## FULLY_QUANTIZED 用谁的 fast dequant:**主力格式用 actlize 的**

`quactlize_mix_gemm_convert.h:38-48` 自己写清楚了:*"actlize's `fast_numeric_conversion_for_mix_gemm.h` defines seven converters... **Not one of them is redefined here**; that header is included below and its converters are used as the vendor wrote them. This file adds the widths GGUF k-quants need."*

| 宽度 | 特化 | 谁的 |
|---|---|---|
| `int4b_t` (8/32) | `MixGemmNumericArrayConverter<half_t,int4b_t,8>` | **actlize,未改** |
| `int8_t` (4/16) | 同上 | **actlize,未改** |
| `uint8_t`/`uint2b_t`/`uint1b_t` | `:447/:470/:492/:557` | **我们的**(vendor 没有这些宽度) |
| native GEMV | `MixGemmByte4ToHalf` | 我们的,但**是 actlize `int8_t` 那条的逐指令复刻** |

**上一轮我说"tensor-core 用 `emit_one`(lop3+fma)"——对 int4 这个主格式是错的。** int4 走 vendor 的:

```
i4s >> 8                                   // 1 条 C 层移位,覆盖 8 个码
ppu.lop3.b32   ×4    (i4s & 0x000f000f) | 0x64006400
ppu.sub.f16x2  ×2    − 0x64086408
ppu.fma.rtte.f16x2 ×2  × 0x2c002c00(1/16) + 0xd480d480(−72)
                     ⟹ 8 条 / 8 个码 = 1 条/code,反量化的一半已含在内
```

`emit_one` 是我们的,只覆盖 vendor 没有的宽度。

## 为什么两条 GEMV 不一样:**不是作者,是表示**

先纠正前提:**代码全是 codex 写的**(我不提交代码文件),git author 三个文件都是同一个,分不出来。

真正的原因在两个签名里,一眼可见:

**native GEMV 吃的是字节对齐的码。** `gguf_vecdot.hpp:495` 的注释明说 *"high bits while they are still **byte-packed**"*,`vecdot_kernel_code4` 做的是 `lo | (high << 2)`(Q3)/`lo | (high << 4)`(Q5/Q6)——**它先把每个码拼成一个整字节**,再把 `uint32_t codes`(4 字节 = 4 码)交出去。`prmt` 只能按字节边界选,所以这条路能用 prmt。

**`gemv_lowbit` 吃的是 sub-byte 的码平面。** `RawConverter<Bits>` 是宽度模板:`(w >> (p*Bits)) & kMask`,`Bits=2` 时一个 word 里 16 个码,`Bits=1` 时 32 个。**prmt 根本够不着**——没有字节边界可选。

所以分岔是 artifact 的形状决定的:native 在上游付了"重组字节"的代价、下游白拿 prmt;`sf-gemv` artifact 故意保持 sub-byte 紧打(那正是它 0.625 B/权重的来源),于是用不了 prmt。

**时间线是个真实的辅因,但不是原因:**

```
gemv_converter.hpp              2026-08-01   ← sub-byte GEMV
gguf_vecdot.hpp                 2026-08-02   ← byte-packed GEMV
quactlize_mix_gemm_convert.h    2026-08-06   ← 共享 converter,比两条都晚
```

写这两条 GEMV 的时候,**还没有可共享的东西**。

## 但这恰恰把 #58 指对了方向

`gemv_lowbit` 用不了 prmt 是对的,**但那不构成用 shift+and+or 的理由 —— 它该用 lop3。**

actlize 的 int4 转换器处理的**就是 sub-byte 紧打的 nibble**:`(i4s & 0x000f000f) | 0x64006400` 一条 lop3 拿两个码、位置不动,高 nibble 的 16 倍在那条**反正要做的** fma 里用 `1/16` 吃掉。零字节对齐要求。

⟹ **`gemv_lowbit` 在 `Bits=4` 上,是在用更差的指令重写 vendor 已经解决的那个问题。** `Bits=2/1` 的对应形式则是我们自己的 `MixGemmChunkEmit` 已经在 fold / 2plane collective 里跑的东西。

**两个机制都已经在树里,一个 vendor 的、一个我们的。缺的是接线,不是机制**([[blocker-mechanism-vs-wiring]])。

（保留范围限制:PPU 上到底几条**没测过**,2.75/对是 sm_120 的。但"源码是 shift+and+or 对 lop3"这一层与编译器无关。）

我把 #58 按这个改写。

```cpp
constexpr uint32_t kMask = uint32_t((1 << Width_) - 1) * 0x01010101u;  // Width=4 → 0x0F0F0F0F
return (word >> Base::shift_of(c)) & kMask;
```

`shift_of(c)` 是**亚字节**移位(Q4_K 高 nibble 就是 4)。**一条移位 + 一条与,把 4 个码同时摊到 4 个字节** —— 一次 SWAR。

GGUF 原生 Q4_K 当然是 2 nibble/byte,和 `sf-gemv` 一样是紧打的。native GEMV 能用 prmt,**是因为它自己先花 2 条指令摊出字节**,不是因为格式送了它这个。

## 重新算账(到"fp16 值、magic 已减",不含 scale 乘)

| | 摊字节 | 转 fp16 | 合计/码 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **native GEMV** | `>>` + `&`(4 码 / 2 条) | 2 prmt + 2 sub | **1.5** |
| **`gemv_lowbit`** | 不摊 | (`>>`+`&`+`\|`) × 4 | **1.5**,而且 magic 还没减 |
| **vendor int4** | 不摊 | 1 `>>` + 4 lop3 + 2 sub + 2 fma | **1.125** |

**两条 GEMV 的每码指令数其实一样。** native 那 2 条 SWAR 正好把 prmt 的便宜吃回去了。

所以机制那句还成立(prmt 确实需要字节边界),但**结论反了**:不是"一条对齐一条不对齐",是**两条都在紧打格式上各走各的绕路,而 vendor 的 lop3 形式两条都赢**。

## 你这个问题还逼出了第三个选项

`sf-gemv` 是**我们离线产的**,所以我们本来就可以**在离线就摊成字节** —— 那样 kernel 里提取是 **0 条**,只剩 2 prmt + 2 sub = **1.0 条/码**,比 vendor 的 1.125 还低。

代价是码平面 int4 → 1 B/码,**翻倍**。而 [[ppu-gemv-alu-bound-not-bandwidth]] 量到 i1/i2/i4 字节差 2.5× 时间只差 1.1% —— 但那是 0.125–0.5 B/码的区间,**1.0 B/码在测量范围外**,是外推不是结论。

⟹ 现在有三条候选,都在树里或都只是离线打包的改动:

```
A  gemv_lowbit 换 vendor lop3 形式            1.125 /码,artifact 不动
B  离线摊字节 + prmt                          1.0   /码,码平面 ×2(带宽外推待验)
C  改吃 native 路(gguf_vecdot)                1.5   /码,但省掉整个 sf-gemv artifact
```

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 01:34 UTC

核完了。**格式对 prefill 不是"较贵",是零成本 —— 而且贵的不是格式,是通用 reader。**

## 为什么 prefill 要这个摆放

因为对 tensor-core 它**没有地址算术**。π = `frag.layout()⁻¹` 把全部索引工作搬到离线:AIU bulk-load 一个 cube 进 shared → swzl 读进寄存器 → **寄存器里的内容直接就是 converter 固定发射顺序期望的那个顺序**。kernel 里 per-code 的地址计算是 0 条。

而且 π **不是自由选择** —— 它是被 converter 的固定发射顺序钉死的(见 [[ppu-swzl-cute-modelable]]:离线重排补偿的是 converter,不是 swzl)。prefill 换个摆放就得付回那笔索引。

## 那 GEMV 为什么贵 —— 不是格式,是 reader

看 `xplane_physical_code` 的核心:

```cpp
int const local = (n % TN) * ArtifactTileK + (k % ArtifactTileK);
int slot = 0;
for (int bit = 0; bit < 14; ++bit)
  if (local & (1 << bit)) slot |= P::get(bit);      // ← GF(2)-线性的位置换
```

**这是一个位置换,不是任意散列。** 在 GEMV 的 k 循环里,`n` 固定、`k` 只有低几位在变,**置换是循环不变量**。现在 `code_at` 每个码重跑一遍这 14 位。

而且**已经有一个反例证明它不必贵** —— `q4_group` 的注释:

> *"An unfolded Q4 placed group is **physically contiguous** but its logical K is an **8x4 transpose**. Vector-load logical x once, read the code group as **four aligned words**, and permute only registers. This is the measured implementation: **per-code inverse lookups were 55x slower**, while this ties raw cold latency at N=K=2048 and wins at saturated N."*

**"physically contiguous" + "permute only registers"** —— 摆放之后码还是连着的,错位只是 8×4 转置,寄存器里换个位置就完了。**格式对 GEMV 是友好的,是通用 reader 没利用这个性质。**

## 所以问题重述

不是"prefill 用了一个对 decode 贵的格式",是:

```
q4_group   unfolded Q4        整字读 + 寄存器置换      已实现,快 55×
code_at    其余全部           每码重跑 14 位置换        出货路的 Q2/Q3/Q5/Q6 和所有 folded
```

**#28 = 把 `q4_group` 那条推广到其余格式和 folded 情形。** 而这在结构上是可判定的,不是赌:π 是显式的位置换对象(`ArrangementSlotPermutation`),"k 的低 b 位是否落在同一个 32-bit 字内"可以**离线枚举验证**,每个 `(Bits, ArtifactTileK, F)` 组合算一次就知道能不能整字读。

⟹ 前一轮我说"② 的提取最贵所以整条线要重定向"—— **方向对,但理由说窄了**。真正的表述是:**出货路上只有 unfolded Q4 走了快读,其余全在通用回退上,而快读的可行性是个可枚举的结构问题,不需要先测。**

要我先把这个枚举做出来吗?（对每个 `(T, ArtifactTileK, High)`,报"连续 CPW 个 k 是否落在同一 32-bit 字 + 字内置换是什么"）—— 这一步纯离线、不用 box,而且直接决定 #28 是"推广"还是"只对部分格式成立"。

理由是你说的那条:一个权重文件。② 读的就是 tensor-core prefill 那份 xplane 摆放;① 要另配原始 GGUF,③ 要另配 `sf-gemv` artifact。而且只有 ② 有 artifact-descriptor 的 ABI。

**2. BACKTEST 里的 GEMV 数全是 ③ 的。**
`D1 16.05 µs / 47.4%` 不是出货 kernel 的数 —— **② 在表里根本没有行**。调优做在了不出货的那条上。

**3. 出货路上贵的是提取,不是反量化。**
② 的转 fp16 已经是 prmt 那条(和 ① 一样)。贵在 `code_at`:每个码重跑一遍 14 位置换 + 自己一次字节载入。对比 ① 的 `extract_word` —— 1 shift + 1 and 出 4 个码。

**4. 格式没问题,reader 有问题。**
摆放对 prefill 是零地址算术(π 把索引搬到离线),而且 π 被 converter 的发射顺序钉死、不能为 decode 改。但摆放是 **GF(2)-线性位置换**,GEMV 的 k 循环里是**循环不变量**。`q4_group` 已经证明了:*"physically contiguous ... read four aligned words, and permute only registers ... per-code inverse lookups were 55x slower"* —— 只是它只覆盖 unfolded Q4。

**5. 可行性可以离线判定,不用上 box。** `ArrangementSlotPermutation` 是显式对象,"连续 CPW 个 k 是否落在同一 32-bit 字"每个组合枚举一次就知道。

**6. 我在这轮说错并已作废三条**:int4 的 fast dequant 是 actlize 的不是我们的;native 也吃紧打格式(它自己花 2 条摊字节);`gemv_lowbit` 不是出货路。

## 确认:不是格式要求的,是 reader 的通用性要求的

摆放把 **`local = (n%TN)·TileK + (k%TileK)`** 当成一个整体坐标做位置换。源码就按这个整体、**每码一次**地应用它 —— 所以地址算术是每码一次。

但 `k` 在一个 4 码组里只动 **2 位**(bit 0–1),另外 12 位(`n%TN` 的 6 位 + `k` 的高 6 位)四个码完全一样;`tn = n/TN`、`artifact_ki = k/TileK`、以及 return 里 `tn·TN·256` 那几项在**整个 k 循环里都不变**。**这些全部被重算了 4 次。**

所以"需要"是个误称。真实的原因是:

> **`code_at` 必须对每一个 `(T, ArtifactTileK, High)` 都正确** —— 包含所有 folded 情形,而每种 arrangement 的置换都不同。写整字读要**逐 arrangement 证明"连续 CPW 个 k 落在同一个 32-bit 字里"**,而这件事只有 unfolded Q4 被证过一次(那就是 `q4_group`)。**通用 reader 是安全形式,不是必要形式。**

而这个证明是可判定的,条件在图里那一行:

```
j = slot % CPW        ← 字内第几个码
slot / CPW 以上       ← 选哪个 32-bit 字

四码同字  ⟺  P::get(0) 与 P::get(1) 都落在 slot 的低 log₂(CPW) 位
```

**只依赖 `ArrangementSlotPermutation`,离线枚举一次就知道每个组合成不成立。** 不用 box,不用先写 kernel。

—— 这正是我给 codex 的第一步:**先出可行性表,再写 kernel。** 表出来之前,"#28 是推广还是只对部分格式成立"是未知的,而这个未知不需要花任何测量成本就能消掉。

解开(codomain 是 `n + 16k`):

```
n = t1 + 8·v2          t = t0 + 4·t1,  t0∈[0,4), t1∈[0,8)
k = 2·t0 + v0 + 8·v1
```

**每个 lane 拿 2 个 n × 4 个 k。同一个 n 的 16 个 k 散在 t0=0..3 这 4 个连续 lane 上。**

## 所以 SIMT 那一半是亏的

```
mma 免费拿到的 k 归约,SIMT 必须自己付:2 × shfl_xor + 2 × add(4-lane 蝶形)
```

```
v.mma m16n16k16   4096 MAC / 条,M=1 时有用的 256 MAC / 条
v.fma.f16x2       32 lane × 2 = 64 MAC / 条
                                        ─────────────
                            mma 仍密 4×,再加归约开销 ≈ 8×
```

(k 是 `2t0, 2t0+1` 相邻,所以 half2 打得满,4 条 hfma2/lane/tile —— 这是 SIMT 最好的情形,不是我给它挑的最坏情形。)

**⚠ 这是指令数比,不是时间比。PPU 上 `v.mma` 与 `v.fma.f16x2` 的发射吞吐比我没测过** —— 若 mma 发射慢 4×,差距就没了。这个数值得单独量。

或者我们理解一下为什么gemv simt现在比tensorcore更快？

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 01:55 UTC

先修premise —— 表里唯一合法的同带对比是 **D1 vs D4**,不是 D1 vs D9:

```
D1  GEMV(SIMT)        16.05 µs   47.4%
D4  tensor-core GEMM  20.74 µs   37.5%    表里自注 "grouped tensor-core GEMM at the same band"
                                          ────────────
                                          SIMT 领先 9.9 点
```
(D6–D9 是 dense-bench,没有 GEMV 对手,不能拿来比。)

## 为什么 —— 三个症状,一个病因

**病因:tensor-core 那条必须假装 M=16,而 decode 只有 M=1。** 三处付账:

**① A 侧 —— 已实测,值 16.9 点**

同一个 config,只换 A 提供者:
```
D7  compact-A capacity 1   26.09 µs   29.1%
D8  ordinary AIU + swzl    16.97 µs   44.7%
D9  PPU_A_PACK cubes       16.49 µs   46.0%
```
**A 的处理方式一项就是 29.1 → 46.0。** 而 GEMV 的 A 是一个广播向量,**成本为零**。这不是假设,是表里的三行。

**② CTA 数不够 —— 结构性**
```
tensor-core  TileN=16/32,N=4096  →  128 ~ 256 个 CTA,每个串行走完 K=4096
GEMV         CtaN=4,N=4096       →  1024 个 CTA,且 K 在 CTA 内按 kThreads 切
```
`gemv_kernel.hpp:40-43` 自陈:*"K IS SPLIT kThreads WAYS ... the epilogue reduces across the CTA. There is no partial buffer, no semaphore and no second kernel — **which is why this covers the decode band without the grouped tensor-core path's split-K machinery**"*。

tensor-core 要拿到同样的并行度得上 split-K(partial buffer + semaphore + 第二个 kernel);GEMV 免费拿到。128–256 个 CTA 在 PPU 上大概就是**一个波以内 ⟹ 整个 kernel 都是 tail**(#10)。

**③ shared 装的是 padding**
```
A-smem  TileM=16 × TileK=256 × 2 B  =  8 KB     其中 15/16 是空的
B-smem  TileN=16 × TileK=256 × 0.5 B = 2 KB     全是有用的
```
**A 占了 4 倍于 B 的 shared,只有 1/16 有用。**

## 所以

**tensor-core 慢的原因不在它读数据的方式 —— 那一半它更好(零 `code_at`、lop3 converter、AIU bulk load)。慢在 M=16 传染到了 A 侧、shared 和调度上。**

这也把你上一个想法收窄了:**"复用加载+dequant,末端换 SIMT"** 里,**换 SIMT 解决不了这三条中的任何一条** —— A 侧、CTA 数、shared padding 全都在 mainloop 之前,与末端用什么算无关。而 SIMT 末端还要倒赔一个 4-lane 归约。

**正确的形式是:保留 MMA,把 M=16 从 A 侧和调度上摘掉。** 那正好是已有的三条:
```
#43  PPU_A_PACK 做成 tactic 轴(D9 证明它值 2.9%,现在不可选)
#45  dense persistent scheduler(在 n-tile 间摊掉 A,小 M 专用)
#10  tail wave ~11%
```

## 还有一个不该漏掉的答案

**M=16 的浪费在 batch≥16 时自动消失。** 单序列 decode 是最坏情形;真实 serving 一批 16 条,tensor-core 那条的 M 就填满了,而 GEMV 得跑 16 遍。

⟹ **"哪条快"依赖 batch,现在的表全是 batch=1。** 这是个比 kernel 优化更早该问的问题 —— 如果出货形态是带 batch 的,那 tensor-core 路本来就该赢,现在的比较是在最不利于它的点上做的。

```
D9  PPU_A_PACK cubes       46.0%
```

**A 的 footprint 直接换算成 blocks/CU。** 记忆里那条 [[ppu-a-must-stay-in-smem]]:A 能从 49152 压到 **768 B**。代进去:

```
每 stage 768 + 2048 + 64 = 2880 B  × s2 = 5760 B
blocks/CU = 262144/5760 = 45  → 被寄存器 28 卡住
⟹ 28 warps/CU  (从 12 涨到 28)
```

**仍然低于 SIMT 的 24–42,但差距从 3× 缩到 ~1.2×。**

## 和上一轮 roofline 的合并

上一轮结论是:**两条路共用同一个 dequant 地板(~11 µs),TC 只免掉 0.5 lane-op/权重。** 现在加上这一层:

> **dequant 的工作量一样,但 tensor-core 路只能派出 1/3 的 warp 去做。**

所以那个 11 µs 的地板**在 12 warps/CU 下够不到** —— 它假设了同样的发射能力。TC 路的真实地板 ≈ 11 µs × (warp 比),而 warp 比正是 A 的 footprint 决定的。

⟹ **#43(A_PACK 做成 tactic 轴)不是 +2.9% 的小优化,它是解开 occupancy 的那把锁。** D9 只测到 +2.9% 是因为它没同时放开 stages/TileK 去把腾出来的 shared 变成 block。

## 一个不能忽略的结构性不对称

**SIMT 完全不需要 staging(32 B);tensor core 必须走 shared** —— AIU→swzl→fragment 这条链是硬件配对的,B 必须先落 shared。所以:

```
SIMT     shared ≈ 0,永远寄存器限,天花板由 R 决定
TC       shared ≥ (A + B + scale) × stages,除非 A 压到极小,否则 shared 限
```

**这不是调参差距,是"用不用 tensor core"自带的。** 唯一的出路是把 A 压到不占地方(#43/#44 已经证明可以到 768 B)。

## 我需要的两个数

```
1  SIMT kernel 的实际 R      编译一次即可(现在是我估的)
2  PPU 的 CU 数量            决定「256 个 CTA 够不够填满机器」
                             ——「grid 不够」和「occupancy 不够」是两个不同的病,
                                现在我分不开
```

第 2 个尤其重要:如果 256 个 CTA 连一个波都不到,那 TC 路的问题**首先是 grid 太小**(TileN=16 太大),而不是 occupancy —— 那样 #45(persistent)比 #43 更该先做。

## 12.4% 就是「每 CU 一个 block」

```
256 线程/block = 8 warps/CTA
理论 37.5% = 24 warps/CU = 3 blocks/CU        (R≤170 正好给 3,与 classic 的 R=170 对上)
实测 12.4% = 7.94 warps/CU

grid 72 × 8 warps = 576 warps
576 / 7.94 = 72.5  ⟹  CU 数 ≈ 72
```

**grid=72,CU≈72 ⟹ 每个 CU 恰好拿到 1 个 block = 8 warps = 12.5%。实测 12.4% 就是它,差的 0.1 是 ramp。**

⟹ **achieved 12.4 vs theoretical 37.5 不是占用率限制器的问题。资源允许 3 个 block,而 grid 从来没要过第 2 个。**

这正是我们**已经记过并在重犯**的那个坑([[ppu-moe-aiu-persist-matches-deepgemm]]):

> *persistent 的 grid 要 **填满 CU 的 slot 数**(`grid = #CU × blk/CU`),**不是每 CU 一个**。*

**grid 应该是 72 × 3 = 216,不是 72。**

## 但先查一件事,否则改了也没用

**tile 队列里有没有 216 个 tile?** persistent 的 grid 再大,没 tile 也是空转。

```
够 216   → grid 是 bug,改完直接 3×,免费
不够      → 病在 tile 粒度(TileN 太大),该动的是分块不是 grid
```

这两条的治法完全不同,而现在分不开。

## instruction fetch 为什么是首位 stall

两个因子相乘,且**都被 12.4% 放大**:

```
① 8 个 warp 盖不住取指延迟     —— warp 少,一个 warp 等取指时没别的可切
② Marlin 主循环展开体大        —— stages × b_sh_wr_iters × n_blocks 全展开,
                                  直线码很长,I-cache 装不下就每轮重取
```

而我们此前量到的「指令数是 classic 的 1.32–2.13×」在这里**第一次变成一等原因** —— 指令多 = 取指足迹大 = 前端压力大。之前它只是个统计事实。

## 一个必须同时测的反向风险

**3 个 block 共用一个 CU 的 I-cache。** 现在 1 个 block 的 8 个 warp 大致同步在同一段码上;放到 3 个 block 后它们会漂开到 3 个不同段:

```
循环体装得下 I-cache  →  warp 多了,取指延迟被盖住,大赚
循环体装不下          →  三份工作集互相冲刷,可能反而更差
```

**所以 grid 修完必须重看 instruction fetch 那一项,不能只看时间。** 这也给了一个能红能绿的判据。

## 顺带,C≈72 把上一轮悬着的两个问题都答了

```
CU = 72,3 blocks/CU  ⟹  216 个 block 槽

tensor-core GEMV  TileN=16, N=4096 →  256 CTA / 216 槽 = 1.19 波
                                       ⟹ 19% 是尾巴  ——  正好是 #10 记的 ~11%
SIMT GEMV         N/CtaN=4 → 1024 CTA,2 warps/CTA,12-21 blocks/CU
                                       ⟹ 864-1512 槽,粒度细得多
```

**「grid 不够」和「occupancy 不够」这两个病,现在分开了:Marlin 得的是前者。**

## 建议的顺序

```
1  查 tile 队列长度                    决定是 grid bug 还是 tile 粒度
2  grid 72 → 216(若 tile 够)          预期 achieved 12.4 → ~37
3  重测 instruction fetch 占比          验证 I-cache 没被冲刷
4  只有 3 通过之后,才谈缩展开体         —— 那时指令数那 1.32× 才是可归因的
```

第 1 步不用跑 kernel,读 scheduler 的 tile 计数就行。

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 02:46 UTC

先更正一个数:**1 block = 8 个 warp,不是 1 个**(256 线程)。所以每个 CU 上有 8 个 warp 可切。

但你的直觉对了关键的一半 —— 只是原因不是"没有别的 warp",而是**那 8 个 warp 是同一个 block 的**。

## 为什么 8 个同 block 的 warp 救不了取指

```
同一个 block  ⟹  被 Marlin 主循环里的 __syncthreads() 拴在一起
             ⟹  8 个 warp 的 PC 几乎相同
             ⟹  它们在同一条取指上一起饿,不是错开饿
```

**切 warp 只有在"别的 warp 有可发射的指令"时才有用。** 而这 8 个都卡在同一段码上等同一批指令 —— 切过去还是没有。

而且取指 stall 和访存 stall **性质不同**:

```
访存 stall   →  warp 多就能盖住(独立的 outstanding load)
取指 stall   →  分两种:
                 延迟型  buffer 空了在等 —— warp 多能盖
                 带宽/容量型  前端本身供不上 —— warp 多反而更抢
```

## 所以 216 之后,是的 —— 但赚的是「跨 block」

```
同 block 的 warp    barrier 耦合,PC 同步,一起 stall
跨 block 的 warp    完全不耦合,PC 自由漂移,stall 相互独立
```

**3 个 block ⟹ 3 条互不同步的指令流。** 一条在等取指时,另外两条大概率在别的位置、有可发射的指令。这正是你说的机制,而且它比"多 8 个 warp"强得多 —— **独立性比数量重要**。

## 但有一个反向风险,必须同时测

```
1 block   1 份 I-cache 工作集(8 warp 同 PC,共享 cache line)   最省 I-cache / 最差隐藏
3 block   3 份工作集(漂开到 3 个不同位置)                      最好隐藏 / 最费 I-cache
```

**Marlin 的主循环是大展开体**(`stages` × `b_sh_wr_iters` × n_blocks 全展开的直线码)。如果它本来就装不下 I-cache,3 份工作集会互相冲刷 —— **1→3 可能变差**。

⟹ 这就是我上一轮说"grid 修完必须重看 instruction fetch 那一项,不能只看时间"的原因。

**判别式(如果 acu 那份报告里有):I-cache 命中率。**
```
命中率高、仍 fetch stall  →  延迟型  →  216 稳赚
命中率低                  →  容量型  →  216 有风险,得先缩体积
```

## 还有一个直接打取指的杠杆,现在才成立

**在 8 warps/CU 下,Marlin 的大展开是在为一个不存在的 regime 买单。**

展开换的是 ILP —— 让单个 warp 内部有更多独立指令可发射。但**前端供不上时,ILP 一点用没有**:你发射不了取不到的指令。

```
高占用 + 前端充裕   展开有意义(隐藏靠 ILP + 多 warp)
12.4% + 取指饥饿    展开纯亏(footprint 变大,ILP 用不上)
```

所以如果 216 之后取指仍是首位,**降 `stages`、降 k 方向展开** 就从"损失流水线"变成"净赚" —— 而这在高占用下是不成立的。

## 收敛成三步,每步有能红能绿的判据

```
1  查 tile 队列 ≥ 216?          否 → 病在 tile 粒度,grid 改了也白改
2  grid 72 → 216               判据:achieved 12.4 → ~37(不是看时间)
3  重看 fetch stall + I-cache   涨了 → 容量型 → 缩展开体
                                跌了 → 延迟型 → 收工,接着看下一个 stall
```

**第 2 步只看 occupancy 不看时间**,是为了把"grid 修对了"和"修对了但被 I-cache 吃回去"分开 —— 否则时间没变会被读成"grid 不是原因",而那是错的归因。

对,而且这句要拆成两个不同的机制 —— 它们的上限和代价完全不同。

## 「增加 grid」有三个来源,只有两个能填 CU 槽

```
① persistent 的 grid 常数    72 → #CU × blk/CU = 216
                             不产生新工作,只是让常驻 block 变多
                             ⟹ 仅当 tile 队列 ≥ 216 才有效

② 更细的 tile(TileN ↓)      N/TileN 增加  ⟹ 真的多出 CTA

③ CTA 级 split-K             把 K 变成并行维  ⟹ 真的多出 CTA
                             代价:workspace + 锁 + 二次归约
```

而 **warp-K(Marlin 的 `NWK`)不在此列** —— 它把 K 分给 CTA 内**已有的** 8 个 warp,不增加 CTA、不增加常驻 warp。它改善的是 CTA 内的延迟隐藏,不是 occupancy。这个区分很重要,别混。

## 关键的算术:M=1 时 tile 根本不够

decode 只有 **N 一个宽维度**。M=1,K 巨大但默认是串行走的。所以:

```
TileN      tiles (N=4096)     对 216 个槽
 128            32              15%
  64            64              30%
  32           128              59%
  16           256             119%
```

Marlin 在 threads=256 下 `n_warps = thread_n_blocks/4`,常见的 `thread_n_blocks=8` ⟹ **TileN=128 ⟹ 只有 32 个 tile**。

**⟹ grid=72 很可能已经超过了 tile 队列。把它改成 216 会完全没有效果。**

这就是我上一轮说"第 1 步先查 tile 队列长度"的原因 —— 现在看,答案大概率是**不够,而且差 6.75×**。

## 所以真正的修法不是 grid 常数

```
1  TileN ↓         直接乘 tile 数;M=1 时几乎免费
                   —— 权重没有 N 方向复用,细分不增加权重流量
                   —— 只多重读 A(K×2B = 8 KB/CTA),256 个 tile 也才 2 MB,
                      对着 8.4 MB 权重可以忽略
                   —— 但注意:Marlin 是寄存器限(R=170→3 blocks),
                      TileN 变小省下的 shared 不会变成更多 block ⟹ 只填满已有的 216 槽,不扩槽

2  CTA split-K     TileN 降到头(=16,256 tiles)还不够时才上
                   Marlin classic 自带(4→2→1 归约 + 锁),但要付 workspace 和 semaphore
                   —— 这正是 SIMT GEMV 用 CTA 内归约免费拿到、而 TC 路要付钱的那个东西

3  grid 常数        等 1/2 把队列填过 216 之后才有意义
```

## 这也把 SIMT 为什么赢讲清楚了

```
SIMT GEMV   grid = N/CtaN = 1024 个 CTA,每 CTA 内再 64 路切 K
            —— 并行度供给充足,且 K 的归约在 CTA 内用 shfl + 32 B shared 解决

Marlin      grid = 32 个 tile,要靠 CTA split-K 才能补,而那要 workspace + 锁
```

**不是 tensor core 慢,是它在 M=1 时的自然分块产生不出足够的 CTA。** 而 SIMT 的分块天生就细(CtaN=4 而不是 TileN=128,细 32 倍)。

## 建议的下一步(顺序不能换)

```
0  读出 tile 队列的实际长度       —— 不跑 kernel,读 scheduler 的计数
                                    这一步决定后面全部
1  若 < 216:降 TileN,重测        判据:achieved occupancy,不是时间
2  achieved 上去之后再看 fetch    涨了→I-cache 容量型,该缩展开体
                                  跌了→延迟型,收工
3  仍不够才上 CTA split-K
```

第 0 步是**唯一一个现在就能做、且能推翻整条推理**的动作 —— 如果队列其实有 300 个 tile,那我上面这一整套就错了,病回到 grid 常数上。

## 队列的迭代空间不是 32 条,是 ~10³ 条

Marlin 的 scheduler 是 **"K-fast stripes + q locks"**,K 是被调度的维度,不是 CTA 内的顺序走法。所以队列长度是

```
(N/TileN) × K-stripes     TileN=128, TileK=64, K=4096  ⟹  32 × 64 = 2048 条
```

**⟹ 我上一轮"队列可能不够 216"的担心大概率不成立。队列很长,grid=72 就是单纯供给不足。**

## 而且这让 grid 72→216 变成免费的

```
每个 tile 仍然只被处理一次          ← 与 worker 数无关
归约次数由「同一 n-tile 有几个 K 段」决定  ← 由分块决定,不由 grid 决定
grid 只改变「同时在飞多少条」
```

**没有额外流量、没有额外归约。纯粹是让 3 倍的 worker 去啃同一个队列。**

⟹ 第 0 步(查队列长度)从"决定性"降级成"确认性"。**主线直接是 grid 72 → 216。**

## 但你这句话真正的分量在这里:两个方向的代价不同

```
N 细分     不同 n-tile 的输出不重叠  →  零归约,免费
K 细分     同一 n-tile 的不同 K 段必须相加  →  q locks + 二次归约
```

所以"造更多 tile"这件事**方向有别**:

```
先 N,后 K。N 到头了(TileN=16)才动 K。
```

而 Marlin 的 split-K 恰恰是 **K 方向**的 —— 它是**有代价的那个**。这也正是 SIMT GEMV 的结构优势:它把 K 切在 **CTA 内部**(64 个线程各拿一段,`shfl` + 32 B shared 归约),**拿到了 K 的并行度而不付跨 CTA 归约的钱**。

⟹ 三条路的并行度供给,代价从低到高:
```
CTA 内切 K      SIMT GEMV 用的        shfl 归约,免费
N 方向细分      两条都能用            无归约
CTA 间切 K      Marlin 用的           workspace + 锁 + 二次归约
```

## 一个新出现的风险

**216 个 worker 抢同一批 q locks,争用可能上升。** 72→216 时锁的持有者变多而锁的数量不变。

⟹ grid 改完要看的**不止**是 occupancy 和 fetch stall,还要看**锁相关的 stall(barrier / 原子)有没有涨**。如果时间没按 3× 改善,这是第一个要查的地方,而不是回头怀疑 grid。

```
1  grid 72 → 216(= #CU × blk/CU)     主线,免费
   判据 achieved occupancy 12.4 → ~37   ← 只看这个,不看时间

2  三项一起复查                        instruction fetch 占比
                                       I-cache 命中率
                                       锁 / barrier stall        ← 新增

3  按 2 的结果分叉
   fetch 涨 + I-cache 跌   → 展开体太大,缩 stages / k 展开
   锁 stall 涨             → 归约成了瓶颈,该往 N 方向细分(免费的那条)
   都没涨、时间也没改善     → 才回头怀疑队列/调度
```

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 02:54 UTC

**有 —— 就是 `warp_k` / `NWK`。上一轮我把 CTA 内切 K 说成 SIMT 独有,错了。**

Marlin classic 里:

```cpp
n_warps = thread_n_blocks / 4;
NWK     = (threads / 32) / n_warps;        // CTA 内的 K 路数
warp_n  = (tid / 32) % n_warps;
warp_k  = (tid / 32) / n_warps;
ktile   = (k % b_sh_wr_iters) * NWK + warp_k;
```
然后一个 `thread_block_reduce` 走 shared 把 NWK 份 fp32 partial 加起来。

## 准确的三层表

```
                     切 K 的位置        归约方式                     路数(threads=256)
Marlin warp-K        CTA 内,warp 间     shared 上的 fp32 partial      NWK = 8/n_warps ≤ 8
Marlin CTA split-K   CTA 之间           q locks + workspace + 4→2→1   由 slice 数定
SIMT GEMV thread-K   CTA 内,thread 间   shfl 蝶形 + 每 warp 1 个 float  kThreads = 64~128
```

**差别是粒度和归约成本,不是有无:**

```
Marlin  ≤8 路,归约要写 shared 再读回   —— 之前 acu 里那个 v.add.f32 20,928 就是它
SIMT    64~128 路,归约是寄存器蝶形     —— shared 只用了 32 B
        ────────────────────────────
        细 8~16×,而且归约不落 shared
```

## 但对 12.4% 这个问题,warp-K 不是解药

```
不增加 CTA        →  填不了空着的 144 个 block 槽
不增加常驻 warp   →  occupancy 不动(warps/CTA 恒为 8,只是分工不同)
warp 仍同 PC      →  被 barrier 拴着,取指仍然一起饿
```

**它改善的是 CTA 内的工作分配,不是 occupancy,也不是取指。**

## 不过它对我们有另一层意义 —— 而且是「还没对齐 marlin」的一条具体内容

我们的 tactic space 里 warp-K **默认是关的**:

```cpp
// ppu_tactic_space.hpp:115-128
warp_k(warp_k_ > 0 ? warp_k_ : tactic_tile_k_)     // 不给就等于 TileK
// :170-175
cta_warps(c) = (tm/wm) * (tn/wn) * (tactic_tile_k / warp_k)
                                    ↑ 默认 = 1,即零个 K cohort
```
而且 `:191-201` 把 WK>1 钉死在 `low_bits==4 && high_bits==0 && fold==1 && b_chunk==0`。

**classic 默认开 8 路,我们默认 0 路,且只有一个格式能开。** 这就是 #57,也是"差异清单"里一条实打实的没对齐。

⟹ 所以 warp-K 该做,但**理由是保真度(对齐 classic),不是 occupancy**。这两件事不要混在一次实验里 —— 否则 grid 改了、warp-K 也改了,achieved occupancy 变了,归因又没法建立。

**顺序:先 grid 72→216(只改一个常数,只看 occupancy),再单独开 warp-K。**

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 03:06 UTC

**方向对,但因果反过来说更准。** 不是"SIMT 能算多个 K",而是 **MMA 强迫一个 warp 算很宽的 n 和 16 个 m,SIMT 可以只算 4 个 n 和 1 个 m —— 于是它剩下的自由度全给了 K。**

## 两个 warp 的 tile 摆在一起

```
                  m      n      k        输出数      有用输出    累加器/线程
SIMT              1      4      1024        4          4         2 个 half2
Marlin            16     64     32        1024         64        32 个 fp32
                  ↑ MMA 的 C fragment 是 16×16,一个 atom 就要 8 个 float/lane;
                    WarpN=64 → 4 个 atom → 32 个
```

**每 warp 每轮读的权重量其实相当**(SIMT 4×1024=4096,Marlin 64×32=2048),**但输出数差 16 倍,累加器也差 16 倍。**

## 三个后果

**① M=1 时那 16 行 m 是白算的**
累加器按 16m 开、A-smem 按 16m 开、MMA 吞吐按 16m 记 —— **只有 1 行有用**。而 `frag_c = 32·MB` 在 `MB=1` 时已经是地板,**降不下去**。这就是 R≈170 → 3 blocks → theoretical 只有 37.5% 的来源。

**② 归约的介质不同**
```
SIMT     shfl 蝶形,寄存器到寄存器,shared 只用 32 B
Marlin   4 个 warp_k cohort 的 fp32 partial 写 shared 再读回
```
之前 acu 里那 `v.add.f32 20,928` 就是后者。

**③ warp 太宽 ⟹ CTA 太少**
Marlin 一个 warp 就吃 64 个 n,一个 CTA 吃 128 个 n。N=4096 只够切 **32 个 n-tile**。SIMT 一个 CTA 只吃 4 个 n → **1024 个 CTA**。

⟹ 这就是 grid=72 那件事的**根**:不是 grid 常数写小了那么简单,是**这个分块本来就产生不出多少 CTA**,只能靠 K-stripe 去凑。

## 一句话说清

**decode 时你只需要 4096 个输出,却必须读 16.8 M 个权重。**

MMA 优化的是**输出吞吐**(每条指令产出 16×16 个结果),而这一端根本不是瓶颈。它为此付出:
```
16m 的累加器和 shared     ← 15/16 浪费
64n 宽的 warp             ← CTA 数不够
shared 上的跨 cohort 归约  ← 比 shfl 贵
```
换来的只是 **0.5 lane-op/权重** 的 MAC 节省(上一轮那个 17–31%)。

**SIMT 之所以在 decode 上更合适,不是因为它算得快,是因为它可以把 warp 做窄 —— 而窄 warp 同时买到了低累加器(高 occupancy)、多 CTA(高并行度)和寄存器内归约。这三样 MMA 一样都给不了,因为它的最小输出块就是 16×16。**

## 于是前面那些数各归其位

```
theoretical 37.5%     ← ① 累加器地板 32 float/线程
achieved 12.4%        ← ③ CTA 少,persistent grid 又只开了 #CU
instruction fetch     ← 8 个 warp 同 block 同 PC,又没有别的 block 可切
dequant 两条一样贵     ← MMA 只免 MAC,不免 ②③ 之外的任何东西
```

**这四条不是四个问题,是同一个:MMA 的最小输出块在 M=1 时太大了。**


## 为什么现在值得重开这个问题

我们记过一条结论([[ppu-aiu-int4-viable]]):**"MoE 该走 AIU,dense 不该 —— 瓶颈是依赖链不是取数"**。

**但那条的前提在这里不成立。** 现在观测到的首位 stall 是 **instruction fetch**,不是依赖链。而 AIU 恰好打在这上面:

```
cp.async.16   每线程每次 16 B    B 每 stage 32,768 B / (16×256) = 8 条/线程/stage
                                 K=4096, TileK=128 → 32 轮 → ~256 条/线程
AIU bulk      整块一条
```

**取指足迹按数量级下降** —— 这正是当前瓶颈的形状。

## 但有一个反向数据点,不能忽略

我们那条 mixed-input WK4 臂**用的就是 AIU**([[ppu-moe-w4a16-cutlass-vs-handwritten]]:*"cutlass collective 也用 AIU bulk load(`copy_aiu`),不是 cp.async"*),而它的指令数是 classic(cp.async)的 **1.32×** —— **更多,不是更少**。

它和 classic 的差异轴太多(converter、投递、epilogue),**不能隔离 load 这一项**。但足以说明"换 AIU 一定减指令"这句话**不成立**,需要实测。

## 代价不只是证明工作量,还有产品面的

AIU 写和 swzl 读是**硬件配对**的([[ppu-swzl-cute-modelable]]),sub-byte 时 B 的字节摆放要补偿 converter 的固定发射顺序。而 Marlin 的卖点之一是:

> [[ppu-marlin-weight-format]]:**vLLM/GPTQ-Marlin checkpoint 的 B 和 grouped scales 都能直接吃,零转换。**

**换成 AIU 就要换 B 的离线摆放 ⟹ 零转换这条没了。**

可以两条并存(`LoadKind` 本来就是 tactic 轴,不同 kind 要不同 artifact),但那意味着**两份权重**或**一次离线转换** —— 这是产品决策,不是 kernel 决策。

## 所以顺序很重要

```
1  grid 72 → 216                achieved 12.4 → ~37.5
2  重看 stall 排序
   fetch 退位了   →  AIU 这条不用做,省一整套 byte/cadence 证明 + 格式代价
   fetch 仍首位   →  AIU 值得做,而且此时它是最直接的杠杆
```

**别为一个可能会自己消失的瓶颈去付 AIU 的证明和格式代价。** 而 grid 那一步只改一个常数。

（另外:AIU 还有第二个可能的收益 —— 它把「取数」从 8 条/线程压成 1 条,顺带**释放寄存器**(不用维持 8 条 in-flight cp.async 的地址状态)。而寄存器正是现在真正的限制器(3 blocks)。这条我没有依据,只是应该一起测的量。）

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 03:59 UTC

这个问题把我的框架修正了一处 —— **12.4% 不是异常,那是 Marlin 的设计点。**

## Nvidia 上 Marlin 也是 1 CTA/SM

```
Nvidia SM 寄存器堆     65,536          (Volta 以来一直是这个数)
Marlin 256 线程 × R≈170 = 43,520
⟹ 65,536 / 43,520 = 1.5  →  1 个 block / SM
⟹ 8 warp / 48(或 64)= 12.5% ~ 16.7%
```

**Marlin 在 5090 上跑的就是 12–17% 的 occupancy。** 它是个 **persistent + 吃满寄存器堆 + 4 级软件流水** 的设计:**用 ILP 和流水线盖延迟,不用 warp 数盖。** `grid = #SM` 是它的本意,不是我们抄错了。

## 但 PPU 的寄存器堆是 Nvidia 的两倍

```
Nvidia   65,536 regs/SM     R=170  →  1 block
PPU     131,072 regs/CU     R=170  →  3 blocks
        ────────────────
        2×
```

**⟹ 照搬 Nvidia 的设计点(1 CTA/CU),在 PPU 上会空掉一半寄存器堆。**

这不是 Marlin 的 bug,是**它的设计点是为寄存器只有一半的机器调的**。我前面说"grid 是 bug",说重了 —— 准确的说法是:**PPU 给了一个 Nvidia 没有的余量,而我们没用。**

## 而取指饿死,说明 Marlin 的赌注在 PPU 上不成立

Marlin 赌的是:**少 warp + 长展开体 + 高 ILP**。这个赌注要求前端能持续供一条长指令流。

```
PPU 相对 Nvidia    寄存器 2×    shared 2.5×(256 KB vs 100 KB)    CU 数 0.42×
前端(I-cache / 取指带宽)         ← 未知,但如果没有同比例放大,
                                   同样的码在 PPU 上就会饿
```

**Nvidia 的 SM 有 4 个 warp scheduler、各自的指令缓冲、以及为这类展开 kernel 调过的 L0I。** 我们观测到 fetch 是首位 stall,恰恰是"这个赌注不成立"的直接证据。

## 于是修法有两条,而且方向相反

```
A  挪到 PPU 的设计点     grid 72 → 216,用满 3× block
                        赚:多 2 条互不同步的指令流
                        赔:3 份 I-cache 工作集 —— 而前端本来就是短板

B  让赌注重新成立         缩展开体(降 stages / 降 k 展开),减小取指足迹
                        赚:前端压力下降
                        赔:ILP 下降,而 Marlin 全靠 ILP
```

**A 和 B 不能同时做**,而且 **acu 里的 I-cache 命中率就是判别式**:

```
命中率高、仍 fetch stall   →  延迟型  →  走 A
命中率低                   →  容量型  →  走 B(A 会更差)
```

## 顺带解释了 SIMT 为什么在 PPU 上赢

SIMT GEMV 是**反过来的设计**:2 warp/CTA、1024 个 CTA、32 B shared、短循环体。

```
它天然吃满 PPU 的宽寄存器堆(高 occupancy)
它的循环体短(前端友好)
它的 CTA 互不同步(stall 独立)
```

**PPU 相对 Nvidia 的三个偏差 —— 寄存器多、shared 多、CU 少 —— 全都利好高占用短体设计,全都不利于 Marlin 那种低占用长体设计。**

## 我不知道的两件事,而它们决定 A/B

```
1  PPU 的 I-cache 大小 / 每 CU 取指带宽     决定 Marlin 的赌注在 PPU 上还成不成立
2  5090 上 decode 时 Marlin 的首位 stall     如果那边也是 fetch,那就是 Marlin 的共性,
                                            而不是 PPU 的短板
```

第 2 条我们**有条件测**(`benchmarks/vllm_marlin_dense_axis_5090.py` 已经在跑 5090 的 Marlin),而它能把"PPU 前端弱"和"Marlin 本来就取指重"分开 —— 这是个很干净的对照,值得先做。

## 三个直接读得出来的事实

**① 取指在 bpc1 上就已经是第一位,占全部 stall 周期的 42.9%。** 不是加了 block 才出现的。

**② 加倍 block,每 warp 的取指 stall 涨了 71.5%。**

这把我上一轮那个判别式回答了 —— 我当时写:

```
延迟型  →  warp 多能盖住,per-warp fetch stall 应当持平或下降  →  走「加 block」
容量/带宽型  →  warp 多互相抢,per-warp fetch stall 上升      →  走「缩指令流」
```

**实测是上升 71.5% ⟹ 前端是供给受限,不是延迟受限。加 block 是错的方向,减指令才是。**

**③ `Not Selected` 从 0 变成 0.256。**
bpc1 下调度器**从来不需要在 warp 之间挑** —— 8 个 warp 没有把发射口填满。这是"1 block/CU 有余量、但前端喂不上"的直接证据,也解释了为什么发射率只涨了 5%。

顺带:**`Stall Tensor Pipe Busy` 两边都是 0**。张量流水线一次都没堵过。

核完了。**你的判断在语义层是对的,而且 `formats.py` 自己就写着理由** —— 但它不是无引用代码,删除会动到路由。

## 为什么没有路径会选它

`quactlize/formats.py:185-200`:

> *"'forbidden' is about STORED bytes... Prefill can convert scales into a transient workspace... **decode cannot, because the planes would have to be resident for every token.**"*
> `fp16_planes="auto"` → `planes_ok = not needs_native_scale(qtype)` —— **对每一个 k-quant 都是 False**

而 `auto` 正是 *"the right default for a resident weight"*。**⟹ 任何 GGUF k-quant 的 decode 都选不到消费 fp16 平面的那条路。** `sf-gemv` artifact 结构性地进不了 decode。

## 一个必须先决定的损失

**BACKTEST 的 D1/D2/D3/D5 是这个 kernel 测出来的**,删掉之后不可复现。而 **D1(16.05 µs / 47.4%)正是今天整场 Marlin-vs-SIMT 比较用的那个 SIMT 锚点**。

两条处理方式,得选一条:

```
   —— 但 bc_vecdot 现在没有基线数(#28 第一步就是补它)
B  先在 box 上补 bc_vecdot 的同 shape 数,再删
```

**我建议 B** —— 否则删完之后我们手上没有任何可复现的 SIMT decode 数,而 Marlin 的对照就悬空了。

#pragma once
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cuda_fp16.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

namespace q4k_gemv
{

struct block_q4_K
{
    half     d;
    half     dmin;
    uint8_t  scales[12];
    uint8_t  qs[128];
};
static_assert(sizeof(block_q4_K) == 144, "block_q4_K must be 144 bytes");
static_assert(sizeof(block_q4_K) % 16 == 0,
              "block stride must be a multiple of 16B: the uint4 loads of the "
              "header and of qs rely on every block being 16B aligned");

constexpr int QK_K               = 256;   // weights per super-block
constexpr int K_SCALE_SIZE       = 12;    // packed (sc, m) bytes per super-block
constexpr int THREADS_PER_SB     = 8;     // lanes cooperating on one super-block
constexpr int BLOCKS_PER_WARP    = 4;     // super-blocks per warp per iteration
constexpr int ELEMS_PER_WARP     = 1024;  // BLOCKS_PER_WARP * QK_K

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// get_scale_min_k4_w: unpack the 6-bit (sc, m) pair of group j.
//
// Same bit layout as get_scale_min_k4() in llama.cpp, but scales[12] arrives as
// three uint32 words and the byte selection is a register shift instead of an
// index into a byte array. Indexing a local byte array with a runtime j would
// force the metadata to memory.
//
// Branch-free: both the j < 4 and the j >= 4 form share the byte index
// i = j & 3 (equal to j when j < 4, to j - 4 otherwise), so the three bytes are
// fetched once, both candidate results are computed, and one is selected.
// A data-dependent branch here would diverge, since lanes 0..3 and 4..7 of a
// super-block group take opposite sides.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
__device__ __forceinline__
uint32_t byte_of(uint32_t w, unsigned i)
{
    return (w >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF;
}

__device__ __forceinline__
void get_scale_min_k4_w(unsigned j, uint32_t s0, uint32_t s1, uint32_t s2,
                        uint8_t& d, uint8_t& m)
{
    // s0 = scales[0..3], s1 = scales[4..7], s2 = scales[8..11]
    unsigned const i  = j & 3;
    uint32_t const b0 = byte_of(s0, i);
    uint32_t const b1 = byte_of(s1, i);
    uint32_t const b2 = byte_of(s2, i);

    uint32_t const d_lo = b0 & 63;                                // j < 4
    uint32_t const m_lo = b1 & 63;
    uint32_t const d_hi = (b2 & 0x0F) | ((b0 >> 6) << 4);         // j >= 4
    uint32_t const m_hi = (b2 >> 4)   | ((b1 >> 6) << 4);

    bool const hi = (j >= 4);
    d = (uint8_t)(hi ? d_hi : d_lo);
    m = (uint8_t)(hi ? m_hi : m_lo);
}

// Four half2 values as named scalars rather than an array: an array written
// through a pointer parameter blocks register promotion and ends up in local
// memory.
struct q_h2x4
{
    half2 q0;   // low  nibbles, elements (0, 1)
    half2 q1;   // high nibbles, elements (0, 1) + 32
    half2 q2;   // low  nibbles, elements (2, 3)
    half2 q3;   // high nibbles, elements (2, 3) + 32
};

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// lop3_convert_to_h2: 32-bit quant word (8 nibbles) -> 4 half2 holding (q - 8),
// with no integer-to-float conversion instructions.
//
// The trick (magic constants from CUTLASS FastInterleavedAndBiased-
// NumericArrayConverter): 0x6400 is the fp16 encoding of 1024, whose mantissa
// occupies the low 10 bits. OR-ing a 4-bit value into that mantissa yields
// fp16(1024 + q) exactly, so one lop3 masks a nibble and inserts the exponent
// in a single instruction, and a following subtract of 1032 = 1024 + 8 leaves
// fp16(q - 8).
//
// High nibbles sit in bits 4..7, i.e. the inserted mantissa is 16*q, so their
// path multiplies by 1/16 and subtracts 72 = (1024 + 8*16)/16 instead, fused
// into one fma.
//
// The leading prmt permutes the bytes [b0,b1,b2,b3] -> [b0,b2,b1,b3] so that
// each output half2 holds two *adjacent* elements. That matches the register
// layout of the float4 activation loads, so the activation side needs no
// packing at all.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
__device__ __forceinline__
q_h2x4 lop3_convert_to_h2(uint32_t i4s_raw)
{
    uint32_t i4s;
    asm volatile("prmt.b32 %0, %1, %1, 0x3120;\n" : "=r"(i4s) : "r"(i4s_raw));

    uint32_t h[4];
    uint32_t const top_i4s = i4s >> 8;

    constexpr uint32_t immLut       = (0xf0 & 0xcc) | 0xaa; // 0xe4 = (A & B) | C
    constexpr uint32_t BOTTOM_MASK  = 0x000f000f;
    constexpr uint32_t TOP_MASK     = 0x00f000f0;
    constexpr uint32_t I4_MAGIC     = 0x64006400;           // half2{1024, 1024}

    asm volatile("lop3.b32 %0, %1, %2, %3, %4;\n" : "=r"(h[0]) : "r"(i4s),     "n"(BOTTOM_MASK), "n"(I4_MAGIC), "n"(immLut));
    asm volatile("lop3.b32 %0, %1, %2, %3, %4;\n" : "=r"(h[1]) : "r"(i4s),     "n"(TOP_MASK),    "n"(I4_MAGIC), "n"(immLut));
    asm volatile("lop3.b32 %0, %1, %2, %3, %4;\n" : "=r"(h[2]) : "r"(top_i4s), "n"(BOTTOM_MASK), "n"(I4_MAGIC), "n"(immLut));
    asm volatile("lop3.b32 %0, %1, %2, %3, %4;\n" : "=r"(h[3]) : "r"(top_i4s), "n"(TOP_MASK),    "n"(I4_MAGIC), "n"(immLut));

    // low nibbles: fp16(1024 + q) - 1032 = fp16(q - 8)
    constexpr uint32_t FP16_TOP_MAGIC = 0x64086408; // half2{1032, 1032}
    asm volatile("sub.f16x2 %0, %1, %2;\n" : "=r"(h[0]) : "r"(h[0]), "n"(FP16_TOP_MAGIC));
    asm volatile("sub.f16x2 %0, %1, %2;\n" : "=r"(h[2]) : "r"(h[2]), "n"(FP16_TOP_MAGIC));

    // high nibbles: mantissa holds 16*q, so scale by 1/16 and offset by -72
    constexpr uint32_t ONE_SIXTEENTH  = 0x2c002c00; // half2{1/16, 1/16}
    constexpr uint32_t NEG_72         = 0xd480d480; // half2{-72, -72}
    asm volatile("fma.rn.f16x2 %0, %1, %2, %3;\n" : "=r"(h[1]) : "r"(h[1]), "n"(ONE_SIXTEENTH), "n"(NEG_72));
    asm volatile("fma.rn.f16x2 %0, %1, %2, %3;\n" : "=r"(h[3]) : "r"(h[3]), "n"(ONE_SIXTEENTH), "n"(NEG_72));

    // uint32 -> half2 reinterpretation: register renaming, no instruction
    union { uint32_t u; half2 h2; } u0, u1, u2, u3;
    u0.u = h[0]; u1.u = h[1]; u2.u = h[2]; u3.u = h[3];
    return { u0.h2, u1.h2, u2.h2, u3.h2 };
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// q4k_dot_word: dequantize one 32-bit quant word (8 weights) and accumulate
// its contribution. All parameters are scalars so the call site can unroll by
// hand; the four accumulators are independent chains.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
__device__ __forceinline__
void q4k_dot_word(uint32_t qword,
                  half2 a_lo0, half2 a_lo1, half2 a_hi0, half2 a_hi1,
                  half2 scale_lo2, half2 zero_lo2,
                  half2 scale_hi2, half2 zero_hi2,
                  half2& dq0, half2& dq1, half2& dq2, half2& dq3)
{
    q_h2x4 const qm = lop3_convert_to_h2(qword);
    // inner hfma2: w = (q - 8) * scale + zero;  outer hfma2: acc += w * a
    dq0 = __hfma2(__hfma2(qm.q0, scale_lo2, zero_lo2), a_lo0, dq0);
    dq1 = __hfma2(__hfma2(qm.q1, scale_hi2, zero_hi2), a_hi0, dq1);
    dq2 = __hfma2(__hfma2(qm.q2, scale_lo2, zero_lo2), a_lo1, dq2);
    dq3 = __hfma2(__hfma2(qm.q3, scale_hi2, zero_hi2), a_hi1, dq3);
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// kernel
//   CTA_N    columns per warp
//   WARPS_N  warp groups along the column axis
//   WARPS_K  warps splitting the k axis inside a group
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
template <int CTA_N, int WARPS_N, int WARPS_K>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(WARPS_N * WARPS_K * 32,
                                  1024 / (WARPS_N * WARPS_K * 32))
q4k_gemv_kernel(
    const half*        act,
    const block_q4_K*  w,
    half*              out,
    unsigned m, unsigned n, unsigned k)
{
    static_assert(CTA_N >= 1 && CTA_N <= 32, "CTA_N out of range");
    static_assert(WARPS_N >= 1 && WARPS_K >= 1, "WARPS_N/WARPS_K must be >= 1");
    static_assert(WARPS_N * WARPS_K * 32 <= 1024, "CTA exceeds 1024 threads");
    constexpr int WARPS   = WARPS_N * WARPS_K;
    constexpr int THREADS = WARPS * 32;

    // Unsigned throughout: signed / and % expand into a sign-correcting
    // sequence, unsigned ones become a single shift or and.
    unsigned const tid        = threadIdx.x;
    unsigned const warp_id    = tid / 32;
    unsigned const lane_id    = tid % 32;
    unsigned const sb_in_warp = lane_id / THREADS_PER_SB;
    unsigned const t_in_sb    = lane_id % THREADS_PER_SB;

    unsigned const n_group    = warp_id / WARPS_K;   // which column group
    unsigned const k_warp     = warp_id % WARPS_K;   // which k slice

    unsigned const row        = blockIdx.x;
    unsigned const col_start  = blockIdx.y * (CTA_N * WARPS_N) + n_group * CTA_N;
    unsigned const blocks_per_row = k / QK_K;

    // Stage the whole activation row in dynamic shared memory. Declared as
    // float4 so the base is 16-byte aligned for the float4 reads below.
    extern __shared__ float4 sh_raw[];
    half* const sh_act = reinterpret_cast<half*>(sh_raw);
    {
        // Cooperative copy, 16 bytes per thread, fully coalesced.
        // k % ELEMS_PER_WARP == 0 implies k is divisible by 8, and the row base
        // is 16-byte aligned, so the float4 view is valid.
        unsigned const n_vec = k / 8;
        float4 const* src = reinterpret_cast<float4 const*>(act + row * k);
        for (unsigned i = tid; i < n_vec; i += THREADS)
            sh_raw[i] = src[i];
    }
    __syncthreads();   // only barrier in the kernel; sh_act is read-only after

    // fp32 accumulator, one per column
    float acc[CTA_N];
#pragma unroll
    for (int ii = 0; ii < CTA_N; ++ii)
        acc[ii] = 0.0f;

    // Strided chunk loop; one chunk is ELEMS_PER_WARP elements of k.
    // WARPS_K need not divide chunks: warps of a group then differ by at most
    // one chunk of work.
    unsigned const chunks = k / ELEMS_PER_WARP;
    for (unsigned chunk = k_warp; chunk < chunks; chunk += WARPS_K)
    {
        unsigned const block_idx = chunk * BLOCKS_PER_WARP + sb_in_warp;

        // ---- stage 1: issue every load first, no arithmetic in between ----

        // Activation: two 16-element runs, 32 elements apart, read from shared
        // memory with absolute k indices (the whole row is resident).
        unsigned const k_lo = chunk * ELEMS_PER_WARP + sb_in_warp * QK_K
                            + (t_in_sb / 2) * 64 + (t_in_sb % 2) * 16;
        unsigned const k_hi = k_lo + 32;

        // Element pairs (2j, 2j+1) already sit in the right register lanes for
        // the half2 arithmetic below, so no shuffling or packing is needed.
        half2 act_lo2[8], act_hi2[8];
        {
            float4 const* src_lo = reinterpret_cast<float4 const*>(sh_act + k_lo);
            float4 const* src_hi = reinterpret_cast<float4 const*>(sh_act + k_hi);
            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(act_lo2)[0] = src_lo[0];
            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(act_lo2)[1] = src_lo[1];
            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(act_hi2)[0] = src_hi[0];
            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(act_hi2)[1] = src_hi[1];
        }

        // Weights: header + quant bytes for every column, back to back.
        // These arrays are only ever indexed by the unrolled loop counter so
        // they stay in registers; spilling them would add local-memory traffic
        // in the hot loop.
        uint4 m4[CTA_N], qs4[CTA_N];
        {
            // Pointer increment instead of a multiply per column.
            block_q4_K const* bq = w + col_start * blocks_per_row + block_idx;
#pragma unroll
            for (int ii = 0; ii < CTA_N; ++ii, bq += blocks_per_row)
            {
                // Header is exactly 16 bytes: d(2) + dmin(2) + scales(12).
                // All 8 lanes of the group read the same address; the hardware
                // merges that into one transaction.
                m4[ii]  = *reinterpret_cast<uint4 const*>(bq);
                qs4[ii] = *reinterpret_cast<uint4 const*>(bq->qs + t_in_sb * 16);
            }
        }

        // ---- stage 2: dequantize and accumulate, no loads ----
#pragma unroll
        for (int ii = 0; ii < CTA_N; ++ii)
        {
            // d, dmin and scales are per (column, super-block). Kept as plain
            // scalars: taking the address of a local would force it to memory.
            uint32_t const meta0 = m4[ii].x;   // d | dmin << 16
            uint32_t const meta1 = m4[ii].y;   // scales[0..3]
            uint32_t const meta2 = m4[ii].z;   // scales[4..7]
            uint32_t const meta3 = m4[ii].w;   // scales[8..11]

            half const d     = __ushort_as_half((unsigned short)(meta0 & 0xFFFF));
            // -dmin by flipping the sign bit, no negate instruction
            half const dminn = __ushort_as_half((unsigned short)((meta0 >> 16) ^ 0x8000));

            unsigned const j_lo = (t_in_sb / 2) * 2;   // group of the low nibbles
            unsigned const j_hi = j_lo + 1;            // group of the high nibbles
            uint8_t sc_lo, m_lo, sc_hi, m_hi;
            get_scale_min_k4_w(j_lo, meta1, meta2, meta3, sc_lo, m_lo);
            get_scale_min_k4_w(j_hi, meta1, meta2, meta3, sc_hi, m_hi);

            // scale and zero in fp16. d8 = 8*d only changes the exponent, so it
            // is exact. zero is a fused multiply-add from (d8, sc): deriving it
            // from the already-rounded scale would multiply that rounding error
            // by 8 and break the (q - 8) anchor cancellation.
            half const d8 = __hmul(d, __ushort_as_half((unsigned short)0x4800));  // 8.0h

            half const sc_lo_h = __ushort2half_rn(sc_lo);   // sc, m <= 63: exact in fp16
            half const m_lo_h  = __ushort2half_rn(m_lo);
            half const sc_hi_h = __ushort2half_rn(sc_hi);
            half const m_hi_h  = __ushort2half_rn(m_hi);

            half2 const scale_lo2 = __half2half2(__hmul(d, sc_lo_h));
            half2 const scale_hi2 = __half2half2(__hmul(d, sc_hi_h));
            half2 const zero_lo2  = __half2half2(__hfma(d8, sc_lo_h, __hmul(dminn, m_lo_h)));
            half2 const zero_hi2  = __half2half2(__hfma(d8, sc_hi_h, __hmul(dminn, m_hi_h)));

            uint4 const qs = qs4[ii];   // 16 bytes = 4 quant words, already loaded

            // Four independent accumulator chains, one per quant word. Written
            // as straight-line code: a loop body containing asm may silently
            // fail to unroll, which would turn the array indices dynamic and
            // push everything into local memory.
            half2 dq0 = __float2half2_rn(0.f);
            half2 dq1 = __float2half2_rn(0.f);
            half2 dq2 = __float2half2_rn(0.f);
            half2 dq3 = __float2half2_rn(0.f);
            q4k_dot_word(qs.x, act_lo2[0], act_lo2[1], act_hi2[0], act_hi2[1],
                         scale_lo2, zero_lo2, scale_hi2, zero_hi2, dq0, dq1, dq2, dq3);
            q4k_dot_word(qs.y, act_lo2[2], act_lo2[3], act_hi2[2], act_hi2[3],
                         scale_lo2, zero_lo2, scale_hi2, zero_hi2, dq0, dq1, dq2, dq3);
            q4k_dot_word(qs.z, act_lo2[4], act_lo2[5], act_hi2[4], act_hi2[5],
                         scale_lo2, zero_lo2, scale_hi2, zero_hi2, dq0, dq1, dq2, dq3);
            q4k_dot_word(qs.w, act_lo2[6], act_lo2[7], act_hi2[6], act_hi2[7],
                         scale_lo2, zero_lo2, scale_hi2, zero_hi2, dq0, dq1, dq2, dq3);

            // Fold the four chains into fp32 once per super-block.
            half2 const s = __hadd2(__hadd2(dq0, dq1), __hadd2(dq2, dq3));
            acc[ii] += __half2float(__low2half(s)) + __half2float(__high2half(s));
        }
    }

    // ---- epilogue: fp32 reduction ----
    // Every lane of the warp holds a partial sum for the same columns, so
    // reduce across all 32 lanes first.
#pragma unroll
    for (int col = 0; col < CTA_N; ++col)
    {
        float v = acc[col];
        v += __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, v, 1);
        v += __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, v, 2);
        v += __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, v, 4);
        v += __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, v, 8);
        v += __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, v, 16);
        acc[col] = v;   // lane 0 now holds this warp's column sums
    }

    if constexpr (WARPS_K == 1)
    {
        // One warp owns the column group outright: store directly, no shared
        // memory and no barrier.
        if (lane_id == 0)
        {
#pragma unroll
            for (int col = 0; col < CTA_N; ++col)
                out[row * n + col_start + col] = __float2half(acc[col]);
        }
    }
    else
    {
        // Combine the WARPS_K k-slices of each column group.
        __shared__ float red[WARPS_N][WARPS_K][CTA_N];
        if (lane_id == 0)
        {
#pragma unroll
            for (int col = 0; col < CTA_N; ++col)
                red[n_group][k_warp][col] = acc[col];
        }
        __syncthreads();

        if (k_warp == 0)
        {
            for (unsigned col = lane_id; col < CTA_N; col += 32)
            {
                float sum = 0.f;
#pragma unroll
                for (int kw = 0; kw < WARPS_K; ++kw)
                    sum += red[n_group][kw][col];
                out[row * n + col_start + col] = __float2half(sum);
            }
        }
    }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// launcher
//   Requires: k % ELEMS_PER_WARP == 0,  n % (CTA_N * WARPS_N) == 0,
//             WARPS_N * WARPS_K * 32 <= 1024
//   Shared memory: k * sizeof(half) bytes for the staged activation row.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
template <int CTA_N, int WARPS_N = 8, int WARPS_K = 1>
void launch_q4k_gemv(
    const half* act, const block_q4_K* w, half* out,
    int m, int n, int k, cudaStream_t stream = 0)
{
    constexpr int WARPS        = WARPS_N * WARPS_K;
    constexpr int THREADS      = WARPS * 32;
    constexpr int cols_per_cta = CTA_N * WARPS_N;
    static_assert(THREADS <= 1024, "CTA exceeds 1024 threads");

    assert(k % ELEMS_PER_WARP == 0);
    assert(n % cols_per_cta == 0);

    dim3 grid(m, n / cols_per_cta);
    dim3 block(THREADS);
    size_t const smem_bytes = (size_t)k * sizeof(half);
    q4k_gemv_kernel<CTA_N, WARPS_N, WARPS_K><<<grid, block, smem_bytes, stream>>>(
        act, w, out, (unsigned)m, (unsigned)n, (unsigned)k);
}

} // namespace q4k_gemv

# Working with codex

## The channel is request/response. Writing is not sending.

codex's process exists only for the duration of a call. `.coord/INBOX.md` is the **persistent record a
call refers to**, not the channel. Anything appended after a call ends sits there with no mechanism
that will ever open it.

**Three levels of evidence. Each licenses exactly one word.**

| you hold | you may say | it proves |
|---|---|---|
| `## NNN` in INBOX.md | **written** | nothing about delivery |
| a dispatch call with a task id | **sent, unconfirmed** | you dispatched |
| `inbox-consumed >= N` in STATUS.md | **read** | codex's own receipt |

Reporting level 1 as level 3 is the single most repeated failure in this collaboration — five times in
one session, with the rule and a CI gate for it already in place. Rules and gates did not stop it; the
judgement criterion does, because it asks *which artifact is in your hand* (checkable now) rather than
*did you remember* (not checkable).

**No task id ⇒ the word "dispatched" is not available to you.**

## Continue the thread; do not start a new one

**Every `mcp__codex__codex` call is a FRESH session.** The returned `threadId` differs each time, so codex's only
continuity is the repository: the code, `.coord/INBOX.md`, and the `.coord/STATUS.md` it writes itself. That is why
the INBOX protocol is load-bearing and why dispatch prompts have to carry so much — they are not verbose, they are
the entire context.

**`mcp__codex__codex-reply` continues a thread** (`threadId` + `prompt`). Default to it. Start a new thread only
when the subject genuinely changes.

**Why it matters more than cost.** A two-phase task — "attack this conclusion, then implement if it survives" —
loses its middle when phase two is a new session: the attack findings have to be re-narrated by you, and
re-narration is exactly where information is lost and where your own summary of someone else's reasoning gets
substituted for their reasoning. Continuing the thread removes you from that seam.

**One reply in flight per thread.** Two concurrent `codex-reply` calls on the same threadId do not queue: codex
answers both in a single turn, that answer is routed to ONE task id, and the other hangs until the 6-hour MCP cap
and reports `failed: timed out`. No work is lost -- the content arrived under the sibling id -- but the failure
looks like a dead codex, and it is a failure mode that the "always continue the thread" default makes MORE likely,
not less. Wait for the notification before replying again; if you must send something urgent mid-flight, put it in
INBOX.md, which is the persistent record that the NEXT turn will read anyway.

**So capture the threadId from every result.** It is in the task notification payload. Without it you cannot
continue, and you will not notice until the moment you want to.

**A fresh thread is not free of risk either:** with no history codex can re-walk a path already rejected. If you
do start fresh, the INBOX item must carry the REJECTION and its reason, not just the current ask — e.g. "F=4 was
once declared dead and that was retracted, so it is uncharted, not disproven."

## Dispatch mechanics that silently do nothing

**The MCP tool's parameters are top-level.** `cwd`, `sandbox`, `approval-policy` are siblings of
`prompt`, not members of `config` (`config` is for `~/.codex/config.toml` overrides). Nesting them
drops all three with no error, so codex runs with defaults while your call reads as if it were
configured.

**`approval-policy: never` means "never ask", which is auto-REJECT.** When codex needs to escalate —
e.g. its sandbox will not start — "never" denies the request. It is not "auto-approve everything".

**`on-request` only helps if the bridge can route the prompt.** Over MCP the escalation may come back
`Rejected("approval request failed")` because there is no channel to a human. Check that before
concluding codex is broken.

**Permissions**: `mcp__codex__*` absent from the settings allow-list means every dispatch waits on a
human click. An unclicked prompt looks exactly like a hung codex from the outside — zero CPU, idle
socket, `inbox-consumed` never moving — because codex received nothing.

## The sandbox, on a container that blocks user namespaces

codex sandboxes commands with **bwrap**. If the container's seccomp filter blocks
`clone(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, bwrap cannot start and **every shell command codex runs exits in 0 ms**,
including the `git pull` it needs to read its own inbox.

Diagnose in one line — `unshare -U true`. "Operation not permitted" with
`/proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces` large and `unprivileged_userns_clone=1` means seccomp, not
sysctl, and it cannot be fixed from inside the container.

The working configuration there is `sandbox: danger-full-access` with `approval-policy: never`, so
codex never needs to ask. **That is a privilege decision belonging to the user**, not one to make
silently; the container being the isolation boundary is an argument to put to them, not a licence.

## `codex exec` as a second channel

`codex exec --sandbox <mode> --skip-git-repo-check - < prompt.txt > log 2>&1 &` has real advantages
over MCP: no client-side approval gate, output streaming to a file you can read at any moment, a pid,
and you can stop it. It hits the same bwrap wall, so it is a different channel and not a different
sandbox.

## Telling "working" from "hung"

**Heartbeats cannot answer this.** codex writes `last-heartbeat` at ITS checkpoints; a process blocked
mid-turn writes none. The instrument goes silent exactly when it is needed.

Two signals from outside, neither needing codex to be healthy:

- **CPU ticks** — `/proc/<pid>/stat` fields 14+15, sampled twice.
- **The socket's timer** — an ESTABLISHED connection with empty queues *and* `timer_active == 0` has
  no retransmit, keepalive or probe scheduled; the kernel will never wake the reader.

**One frozen window is not a hang.** A live codex was measured using **~4.5 s of CPU across twenty
minutes** — it wakes per streamed chunk and sleeps between. A five-second sample landing in a gap sees
exactly what death looks like. Require the state across several windows *and* zero cumulative CPU over
the whole span; a gap cannot survive the span because the next chunk lands inside it.

**Two more traps in writing such a probe:** matching `codex` anywhere in a cmdline makes the probe
match *itself* (a liveness check that cannot fail); and taking the top-N processes by total CPU can
miss a freshly-started one. Match `argv[0]`.

**And the verdict must not name a cause.** "CPU frozen, socket idle and untimered" is produced
identically by *a reply that will never arrive* and *a request that was never delivered*. Call it
STALLED, not HUNG, and check the cheap cause (permissions) before the expensive one (a dead peer).

`ci/codex_liveness.py` in quactlize implements all of this.

## The MCP wrapper carries a fuse, and it kills a HEALTHY turn

**Observed 2026-08-12.** codex had been working for three hours — seven commits, gates green,
mid-derivation on the load-bearing seam. Then, with no warning in its own log:

    turn_aborted   reason=interrupted   duration_ms=10818891   (3.005 h)

Nothing was wrong with codex. **Every `codex-reply` leaves a background wrapper whose tool timeout is a
fuse, and when the fuse burns down it aborts whatever turn is running.** `TaskStop` on that wrapper does
the same thing. The fuse is not per-turn: it starts when the wrapper starts and can span several turns,
so the turn it kills is usually not the one that lit it.

**Where it is set:** `~/.claude.json` -> `mcpServers.codex.timeout`, milliseconds. It shipped here at
`21600000` (6 h).

**Do not delete the field to disable it** — the fallback default is far SHORTER, so deleting makes every
turn die sooner. Raise it (`604800000` = 7 days). **The new value only takes effect on the next Claude
Code start**, so the running session keeps the old fuse; plan the night around the old number.

**This is not the same setting as `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`.** That one is about silence
between chunks and is already `0` here. A wrapper that is streaming happily still burns its fuse.

### The fix: run the thread over `codex exec resume`, not the MCP tool

**Verified 2026-08-12, not theorised.** After four aborts in one evening — 3.01 h, 2.72 h, then 42 s
and 24 s for two restarts that the next fuse killed on arrival — the thread was moved to the CLI:

    cd <repo>
    codex exec resume <session-uuid> \
      --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --skip-git-repo-check \
      -o <last-message-file> -  < prompt.txt

**Same session id, so the whole conversation carries over** — this is not a fresh thread. And there is
no MCP wrapper, so there is no fuse. A fifth fuse fired eighteen minutes later and the CLI turn kept
running through it, which is the actual proof.

Two flag placement traps: `resume` does **not** accept `-C/--cd` (put the process in the repo with
`cd` instead), and the global options must sit **after** `resume`, not before it.

**When several fuses are queued, restarting over MCP is a losing game.** They were all created inside a
three-minute window hours earlier and burned down one after another, each killing whatever turn was
running — including the restart sent seconds before. Switch channels instead of retrying.

**Stop the surviving wrappers while codex is idle.** `TaskStop` aborts a running turn, so the moment
right after an abort — or right after a fresh turn starts, when losing it costs a handful of events —
is the cheap window. Leaving one alive means it fires later, on a turn holding hours of work.

### The probe must distinguish three states, not two

`turn_aborted` and a genuine hang look identical from the outside — in both, the event log stops
growing. They need opposite responses, so a probe that only knows "done / not done" is not enough:

| exit condition | what actually happened | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| `task_complete` appears | the turn **finished normally** | review, then dispatch the next turn — codex is stopped and INBOX is unread by construction |
| `turn_aborted` appears | something **outside** killed a healthy turn | resend `codex-reply` immediately; the uncommitted work is usually still on disk |
| N minutes with no new event | possibly hung — see the section above | diagnose before resending |

**A probe must notify by EXITING, not by printing.** Background output is not read unless something
brings you back; only the process ending does that. A long-lived probe that prints status forever is
indistinguishable from no probe — that mistake cost four hours of codex idling once already. Poll on
the order of minutes, not tens of minutes: a long interval saves nothing and converts "it stopped" into
a whole idle block.

### The two channels fail in opposite ways — and there is a fourth state

Neither channel is strictly better; they trade one failure for another, and knowing which you are on tells
you what to watch for.

| | MCP `codex-reply` | `codex exec resume` |
|---|---|---|
| carries the 6 h fuse | **yes** — kills healthy turns | no |
| survives a Claude Code restart | the server does, but… | **no** — it is a child process and dies with the parent |
| resumes a thread after **its own** process restarts | **no** — `Session not found for thread_id`, the mapping was in memory | **yes** — reads the rollout file from disk |

Observed both in one night: the fuse killed four MCP turns, so the thread moved to the CLI; then the
Claude Code process restarted, the CLI child died with it, and the MCP server had also restarted so
`codex-reply` answered `Session not found`. Only `codex exec resume <uuid>` could pick the thread back
up, because the on-disk rollout is the durable copy.

**This adds a fourth state the probe must separate**, and it is the one that looks most like a hang:

| what you see | what happened |
|---|---|
| `task_complete` in the log | finished normally |
| `turn_aborted` in the log | interrupted, marker written |
| log stopped, **process alive** | genuinely hung — diagnose before resending |
| log stopped, **process gone, no marker** | **killed** — the log simply ends mid-turn |

The last two are indistinguishable from the log alone. The discriminator is whether the process still
exists, so a probe that only reads the transcript cannot tell them apart and will sit through a dead
session waiting for events that will never come.

Match `argv[0]`/`argv[1]` when checking, not a `-f` pattern: `pgrep -f 'codex exec'` matches the shell
running the check, so the liveness test can never fail. `ps -eo args --no-headers | awk '$1 ~ /codex$/ && $2 == "exec"'`
does not have that problem.

### After an abort, the work is on disk

An aborted turn does not roll back the worktree. Everything codex had written but not committed is
still there. **Before anything else, tell codex its work survives and have it commit with explicit
pathspecs** — and say plainly which parts are unfinished, so nothing half-done is committed as
complete. Do not commit it yourself; see the worktree rules below.

The restart prompt must also say **that the abort was external**. Otherwise codex reads the gap as its
own failure or as the task being cancelled, and re-derives what it already had.

## Sharing one worktree

**Never `git add -A`.** The ownership split is agreed at the level of *editing*; `-A` ignores it at the
level of *committing* and sweeps codex's in-progress files — possibly mid-edit — into a commit whose
message describes something else. `git add <explicit paths>` and read `git status --porcelain` first:
a path outside your half means codex is working, not that you should include it.

**If you already did: do not rebase.** codex is running; rewriting history under it is worse than a
wrong message. Append an INBOX item saying which item was committed, telling it not to redo the work
and to check whether what landed is what it intended.

`.coord/STATUS.md` is codex's file. Committing it yourself destroys the receipt your own delivery
criterion depends on.

## Getting useful work back

- **Ask for a commit per sub-item.** "Commit after each of ①②③ rather than batching" makes progress
  observable without codex having to report it, and gives a second cheap liveness signal.
- **Ask it to write `inbox-consumed` before starting work**, not after finishing.
- **Send one item, not four.** A dispatch that also says "and read this whole third-party source tree"
  is one you cannot distinguish from a stall.
- **Tell it what you changed on your side**, including things it did not ask about. It reads the repo,
  and an unexplained rename reads as breakage.
- **Give it the design input rather than the design.** Pointing at
  `Kernels/general/w4a16_gemm/fpA_intB_standalone/` and naming the field
  (`enableCudaKernel`, first in the record, tile fields meaningless when set) got that encoding back
  verbatim, better documented than the request.

## codex is often right

In one session it overturned five of my blocking judgements, each time correctly: a format that was
already supported by a trait-driven collective; a builder that already routed a case I said it did
not; a fault-injection heuristic that would have hit the wrong tensor. **It is in the files and you
are not.** A "this is impossible" derived by reasoning should be assumed wrong until it has been read
off the object. See `blocker-mechanism-vs-wiring`.

Align on decisions and commits with codex *before* reporting to the user; give the user the
synthesised conclusion, not the negotiation.

## Traps this collaboration actually hit (2026-08-07)

Nine of these are mine, and eight of the nine share one root: **I concluded from an instrument I had not
checked.** The tenth is codex's and it is the same shape. Each entry gives the judgement that catches it *before*
the conclusion leaves your mouth.

### Writing is still not sending

I unblocked codex with a commit, wrote "you can proceed" into INBOX, and never dispatched. codex sat idle at
`inbox-consumed: 088` while I reported it as working. The rule at the top of this file already says this; having
the rule did not stop it, because the failure happens at a moment when you *feel* you have communicated.

**Judgement:** before saying codex is doing anything, name the task id from the dispatch call. No id, no verb.

### The shared container

codex and I share `/tmp`. I ran `g++ ... | head -5 && /tmp/sc` — the compile FAILED, `head` returned 0, `&&`
fired, and `/tmp/sc` **existed because codex had built it**. I nearly reported codex's probe output as my own
measurement.

Two rules, both cheap: **never read success through a pipe** (`cmd | head` reports head's status, and this
repository has now paid for it four times), and **name scratch binaries uniquely** (`/tmp/claude_<thing>`).

### Reproduce a gate's failure WITH the gate

The syntax tier reported 40 `mixed policy` assertions on `test_int1_sweep.cu`. I hand-rolled an nvcc line, got 0
at the base revision, and announced twice — with different attributions — that codex's commits had introduced it.
codex re-ran **the actual gate** in a clean worktree at the same base and got the same 40. It was pre-existing;
my command simply did not carry the gate's flags.

**Judgement:** a hand-rolled repro of a gate failure is a different experiment. If you must hand-roll, say so and
do not attribute. Attribution requires the gate, at a sha, in a clean tree.

### Gate results need a sha (and a clean tree)

On a shared worktree, `local_gates` measures a state that is **nobody's commit**. codex reported "4 reds are
pre-existing" from its own dirty tree; I reported an attribution from mine. Both unfalsifiable.

`git worktree add -q --detach /tmp/wtX <sha>` is the whole fix. Remove with `--force` and `prune` afterwards, and
**do not cd into it before removing** — getcwd fails.

To codex's credit it later re-ran four gates properly and replaced its own sloppy claim with a precise
classification: two stale gates, one stand-in-environment failure, one checker false positive. **That is what a
retraction should look like**, and it is worth asking for in those terms.

### Do not file your own action items into codex's queue

My review of #44 ended in "there should be a gate that compiles at each R", and I sent that to codex along with
the finding. `ci/` is mine. A review conclusion whose action lands in your own half is work, not a request.

**Judgement:** after every review, sort the conclusions by whose files they touch before writing the INBOX item.

### Run their test the way their test runs

codex added `tests/test_moe_only_filter.py`. I ran `python3 tests/test_moe_only_filter.py`, got rc=0 with the
regression re-injected, and was one sentence from reporting "the gate is empty". It is a pytest module: running
it directly imports and exits. Under `pytest` it fails correctly on the injected regression.

**Judgement:** an rc=0 from a test you invoked a new way is not evidence until a **negative control** fails.
Inject the exact defect the test was written against; if it still passes, THEN you have a finding.

### Fit against the variable the machine actually consumes

I fitted `t = a + b·W` with `W` = useful FLOP across two token counts and derived "723 µs of fixed per-call
overhead". The machine does *padded* work, and `msk` fell 14.5% → 5.4% between the points, so `mt` grew 3.62×
while useful FLOP grew 4×. Using `mt`, no intercept is needed. A later M=1 run took 20.8 µs total — an order of
magnitude below the "constant" — which falsified it outright.

**Judgement:** before fitting, ask which quantity the hardware is proportional to. Two collinear terms cannot be
separated by two points, and a fit will happily invent a constant to absorb the difference.

### A probe that trips over the thing it is probing

To measure what relaxing `ScaleCopyCoverage` would open, I wrote a probe that skipped that exclusion — but its
first line called `kernel_exclusion()`, which is **where the exclusion lives**. It returned early, my skip never
ran, and I reported "+0%, relaxing buys nothing". The real answer is +48% to +99%, and it recovers a warp shape
that is otherwise 0 rows.

**Judgement:** when a probe reports "no effect", the first hypothesis is that the probe did not reach the
subject. Prove the bypass fires — print the count of rows that took it.

### Verify a command before handing it over

I gave a build command containing `MOE_STAGES=6`. That variable exists in exactly two strings, both of which
*advise using it*, one printed by the build itself; nothing forwards or reads it. I also guessed the binary path
when `build.sh` finds and prints it.

**Judgement:** every knob in a command you hand over must be traceable to a forwarder or a cache var, and every
path to something that printed it.

### The class these keep landing in

Four separate checks this session hardcoded a property of their subject and reported the mismatch as the
subject's fault: the units gate spelled six `[0-9]+` and said "the table declares 404"; the provenance gate
hardcoded a macro prefix and said grouped tables "predate the durability guard"; `generated-edges` resolved
build-dir output against the source tree and said "the generator will emit a source that cannot compile"; and the
tactic space encodes a scale-copy constraint so a legal warp shape is never emitted at all.

**Judgement:** when a check's message blames the artifact, read the check first. And prefer a `static_assert` in
the kernel over a rule in the enumerator — the enumerator makes "lost" and "never generated" identical.

## 取指 stall 需要两个条件**同时**成立

```
①  warp 准备好发射        —— 没被数据/访存/barrier 挡住
②  下一条指令不在缓冲里    —— 静态足迹大到装不下 / 流式走过
```

```
GEMV     ①  成立   ALU 受限,一直在发(i1/i2/i4 三个位宽全落 ~16.0 µs,字节差 2.5× 时间差 1.1%)
         ②  不成立 循环体小,第一遍之后全命中
                    ⟹ 不 stall

Marlin   ①  成立   DRAM 才 16.72%,根本不在等内存
         ②  成立   主循环全展开,一遍走过就不再回头
                    ⟹ 42.9% 的 stall 周期都在这里
```

**指令多 ≠ 取指压力大。决定取指的是「静态足迹 / 复用距离」,不是「动态条数」。**

## 两者的形状差在哪

```
GEMV     滚动循环
         ┌──────┐
         │ 体   │ ←──┐     复用距离 = 体长(~10² 条)
         └──────┘    │     每轮重新走同一批 cache line ⟹ 命中率 ~100%
             └───────┘

Marlin   全展开   stages(4) × b_sh_wr_iters × NBlocks × dequant
         ├────────────────────────────────────────────┤
          ↑ 一遍走过,体内部零复用                    ↑
         复用距离 = 整个展开体(~10³ 条)
```

从 acu 反解 Marlin 的密度:

```
每 warp 指令数    1,826,440 / (72 CTA × 8 warp) = 3,171
每 warp mma 数    65,536 / 576                  = 113.8
每条 mma 的指令   3,171 / 113.8                 = 27.9      (其中 dequant 占 12)
```

一个 TileK 步 = 8 条 mma ≈ **224 条直线码**;若 `stages=4` 也展开 ⟹ **~900 条**。而 GEMV 的循环体是 10² 量级。**差一个数量级,而且 Marlin 那 900 条内部一条都不复用。**

## 这个对比顺带答了「容量型还是带宽型」

上一轮我说要 I-cache 命中率才能分。**GEMV 这个对照本身就是一半的判别式:**

```
若是纯带宽型(前端发射口窄)  →  GEMV 也在满发射,也该 stall
                              但它不 stall
⟹ 光有「发射密」不够,还要「足迹大」  ⟹  是足迹/容量这一侧
```

严格说不能完全排除带宽(GEMV 的足迹小到根本不产生取指请求,所以它对带宽的需求本来就低),但**方向已经指向足迹**。

## 一个反直觉的推论,值得先说清楚

**杠杆不是「减少指令」,是「缩小静态足迹」—— 而这两件事可能反向。**

```
把展开的循环重新卷起来:
   动态指令数  ↑   (多了循环计数器和分支)
   静态足迹    ↓↓  (体积除以展开倍数)
   ILP         ↓   (Marlin 的全部本钱)
```

**⟹ 修完之后 acu 上的指令总数可能变多,而时间变短。** 如果按「指令数降了没」判读,会得出相反结论。判据必须是 **fetch stall 占比 + I-cache 命中率**,不是指令数。

而 ILP 那一项的损失现在**不像以前那么贵** —— 因为 `Not Selected = 0` 说明 bpc1 下发射口根本没填满,ILP 买来的并行度没人消费。

## 一个不用上 box 就能量的东西

上面「10² vs 10³」是我从每-mma 密度推的,不是量的。**直接量:**

```bash
nvdisasm <marlin binary>  →  数主循环那段直线码的静态条数
nvdisasm <gemv binary>    →  数循环体的静态条数
```

这把「足迹差一个数量级」从推理变成读数,而且**不需要跑 kernel、不需要 acu**。如果差距其实只有 2-3×,那我上面这套解释就站不住,得回头找别的原因。

---

一点交代:**「GEMV 不 stall 在取指」这条是你的观测,不是我手上的数据。** 我们的 BACKTEST 里 GEMV 只有时间和 %HBM,没有 warp-state。上面整套推理建立在你那个观测上 —— 如果 GEMV 的 acu 也在手边,值得把它的 Warp State 也转录出来,那样这个对比就有两侧的数了。

## 展开在哪:`marlin_collective_ppu.hpp` 的四层嵌套

```cpp
while (k_tiles_remaining > 0) {                          // :535  ← 唯一卷着的一层
  #pragma unroll
  for (int pipe = 0; pipe < Stages;) {                   // :536-537  ×4   Stages=4
    #pragma unroll
    for (int inner = 0; inner < BInnerIters; ++inner) {  // :538-539  ×2   BInnerIters=2
      load_registers(inner + 1, pipe % Stages);          // :540  → :484-505
      if (inner == BInnerIters - 2) {
        copy_stage(...); ++pipe; wait_stage();           // :542  → :456-482
      }
      multiply(inner);                                   // :548  → :507-518
    }
    --k_tiles_remaining;
    if (k_tiles_remaining == 0) break;
  }
  a_pointer += AGlobalOuter * Stages;
}
```

而 `multiply` 里是**手写四份,不是循环**(:508-517):

```cpp
// "Spell the four compile-time N blocks explicitly."
multiply_n_block<0>(...);  multiply_n_block<1>(...);
multiply_n_block<2>(...);  multiply_n_block<3>(...);     // ← 第四层展开
```

**直线体 = Stages × BInnerIters × 4 个 n-block = 4 × 2 × 4 = 32 条 mma。**

## 两条独立推导对上了

```
从源码结构   直线体 32 条 mma
从 acu       每条 mma 27.9 条指令(3,171 指令/warp ÷ 113.8 mma/warp)
             ─────────
             32 × 27.9 = 893 条直线码       ← 与我上一轮独立估的 ~900 一致
```

再交叉核一次「进入次数」:

```
从 acu       113.8 mma/warp ÷ 32 mma/体 = 3.56 次
从调度       (32 n-tile × 32 k-tile) ÷ 72 CTA ÷ Stages 4 = 3.56 次   ✓ 精确相等
```

**⟹ 一个 893 条的直线体,每个 warp 只进 3.56 次。** 冷取指几乎摊不掉 —— 这就是取指占 42.9% 的直接来源。对比之下,滚动循环的体虽然也要冷取一次,但它进几百次。

## 哪一层能动,哪一层不能

关键区分:**`pipe` 只索引 shared 指针,`inner` 索引寄存器数组。**

```cpp
// pipe 的全部用途 —— 都是指针偏移
shared.a     + ASharedStage * pipe          // :458, :490
shared.b     + BSharedStage * pipe          // :462, :502
shared.scale + ScaleSharedStage * pipe      // :472, :486
a_pointer[AGlobalOuter * a_offset]          // :461   a_offset = pipe

// inner 的全部用途 —— 都是寄存器数组下标
fragment_a[inner & 1]                       // :494, :510-517
fragment_b_quant[inner & 1]                 // :503
fragment_scale[inner & 1]                   // :487, :510-517
state.a_smem_read[inner % BInnerIters]      // :495, :499
```

**⟹ `:538` 的 inner 展开是承重的**(卷起来 `fragment_*` 会掉进 local memory,正是那份参考 kernel 注释里反复警告的失败形态)。

**⟹ `:536` 的 pipe 展开不承重。** 把它改成 `#pragma unroll 1`:

```
直线体      893 → 223 条        4×
语义        不变(Stages / BInnerIters / 输出映射 一个没动)
寄存器      预期不变(pipe 不索引任何寄存器数组)
证明门      不触发 —— PipelineDepthUnproved 管的是 Stages 的值,不是它展不展开
```

**这是目前唯一一个能缩静态足迹、又不用先还任何证明的杠杆。** 其余三层都被门挡着:

```
Stages=4 改小            PipelineDepthUnproved("only the classic four-stage cadence is proved")
4 个 n-block 改少        ClassicOutputMapUnproved(wn 必须 64)
BInnerIters              = BSharedStage/Threads,由 TileN/TileK/Threads 导出,不是独立旋钮
```

## 要注意的两个风险

```
1  跨 pipe 迭代的软件流水会丢
   编译器现在能在 4 份 pipe 之间调度 copy/wait/mma;卷起来就只能在一份内部调度。
   ILP ↓ —— 但 Not Selected=0 说明 bpc1 下发射口本来就没填满,这个损失可能收不到。

2  __syncthreads() 进入卷起来的循环体
   wait_stage() 里有 barrier(:481)。inner 仍全展开 ⟹ 条件 inner==0 是编译期常量
   ⟹ barrier 调用仍然一致,不会分叉。但值得在 acu 里看 Stall Sync 有没有变。
```

```
I-cache 命中率(若有)         ←  这条才分得开容量型和带宽型
Stall Sync                   23.6%  →  ?   (风险 2)
Regs / spill                 124    →  ?   (风险:pipe 卷起来若意外产生 spill,立刻作废)
时间                         16.96 µs → ?
```

## Assistant · 2026-08-14 07:49 UTC

读了两个。**是三种机制,不是两种,而 Marlin 的是串行度最高的那个。**

## 三者并列

```
                   Marlin C-chain          actlize stream-K         actlize separate-reduction
partial 存哪       没有 workspace          FP32 workspace           FP32 workspace
                   直接改 D                (一块,累加)             (每 peer 独立一块)
CTA 间等待         wait_eq(peer_idx)       wait_eq(K_idx)           不等
                   严格串行链              等前序 K split 加完       只 arrive_inc(1)
推进量             +1(一个 peer)         +k_tile_count            +1
归约在哪           producer 里边算边加     producer 里              第二个 kernel
流量               最小(只有 D)          partial 写 + 读          partial 写+读 + 一次 launch
状态               在用                    在用                     被关闭了
```

## Marlin 的设计是明写的:它**没有** FP32 workspace

```cpp
// marlin_scheduler_ppu.hpp:25-28
// Its workspace is one CTA-wide lock per global output-tile q.  In particular, it has
// no accumulator type and cannot name, allocate, or index an FP32 partial tile:
// the standalone cooperative hands partials through its own Marlin C-chain protocol.
```

协议就是一条链(`:436-464`):

```cpp
acquire:  Barrier::wait_eq(locks, tid, lock, work.peer_idx);   // 等 lock == 我的编号
release:  if (final_peer) locks[lock] = 0;                     // 最后一个复位
          else Barrier::arrive_inc(locks, tid, lock, 1);       // 否则放行下一个
```

**peer 0 → 1 → 2 → … 严格按序。** peer k 的 epilogue 必须等 0..k-1 全部做完。partial 走 D 本身,所以流量最小 —— **代价是把并行度换成了一条链**。

而 actlize 等的是 `K_idx`、推进 `k_tile_count`(`:533,:544`),粒度是 K split 不是 peer;**它的 `separate_reduction` 分支根本不等**(`increment = 1`,每 peer 写自己的位置)。

⟹ **codex 提的「独立 partial + 第二次归约」就是 actlize 的 `separate_reduction`,机制已经在,只是关着。** 它自己也点了这句(`:533` 那个引用)。

## 但今天更要紧的是:**TileN 和 split-K 深度不是两个独立的轴**

```
Marlin  TileN=128  →  N=4096 只有 32 个 n-tile  →  填不满 72 个 CU
                   →  必须深切 K            →  每个输出 tile 一条长 peer 链
                   →  Stall Sync 23.6%,lock polling bpc1→bpc2 从 1,299 涨到 9,653

D9      TileN=16   →  N=4096 有 256 个 n-tile  →  够填满
                   →  几乎不用切 K          →  没有链,没有锁
```

**⟹ Marlin 的 TileN 选择把它的 scheduler 逼进了串行 regime。** 这两个不能分开归因。

而这正好补上了 46.0% → 18.5% 那个九轴差集里我一直没说清的一环:

```
Instruction Fetch  42.9%   ← 893 条展开体(TileN=128 → WarpN=64 → 4 个 n-block 手写)
Stall Sync         23.6%   ← peer 链(TileN=128 → n-tile 少 → 必须深切 K)
                   ─────
                   66.5%   两者都是 TileN=128 的下游后果
```

**两个最大的 stall 都追溯到同一个选择。**

上一轮那个梯度里,**步骤 ①④(动 TileN)会同时改变 split-K 深度**。必须把它记成两列而不是一列:

```
D9              16      256         ~1             1           46.0
```

三个来源,而且**我之前把它整个归给 peer 锁链是错的**。

## 三处 sync

**① 流水线 barrier — `marlin_collective_ppu.hpp:479-482`**
```cpp
auto wait_stage = [&]() {
  marlin_ppu_detail::cp_async_wait<Stages - 2>();
  __syncthreads();
};
```
调用点:prologue `:524` 一次,主循环 `:546` 每个 pipe 迭代一次。

**② peer 锁 — `barrier.h:151-162`(`wait_eq` 里就有 barrier)**
```cpp
if (thread_idx == 0) { #pragma unroll 1 while (ld_acquire(flag_ptr) != val) {} }
Sync::sync();          // ← __syncthreads,255 个线程停在这
```
**只有 thread 0 自旋,其余 255 个停在 barrier 上** —— 所以锁链**确实**计入 Stall Sync,不是计入 Memory Dependency。

**③ release 之后的 result-staging barrier**(`:455-457` 注释提到)。

## 但数一下,主循环才是大头

```
s.blksyn.defer  13,408(bpc1)  ÷ 576 warp  =  23.3 次/warp

主循环   wait_stage × (Stages 4 × while 3.56) + prologue 1  =  15.2      65%
其余                                                  23.3 − 15.2 = 8.1   35%
                                                      ← epilogue:wait_eq 的 Sync + staging
```

**⟹ 约 65% 的 barrier 是流水线的 `wait_stage`,不是 peer 锁。** 我上一轮说「Stall Sync 23.6% ← peer 链」是错的归因。

每次 barrier 的代价:
```
每 warp 总周期    3,171 × 2.1497 = 6,817
其中 Sync         3,171 × 0.5072 = 1,608
每次 barrier      1,608 / 23.3   =  69 周期
```

## 更要紧的一层:访存延迟被**转换**成了 barrier 等待

```cpp
cp_async_wait<Stages - 2>();   // ← 先等自己的异步拷贝  → Stall AMC 9.1%
__syncthreads();               // ← 再等最慢的那个 warp → Stall Sync
```

8 个 warp 里只要有一个的 copy 没回来,**其余 7 个的等待就记在 Stall Sync 上而不是 Memory Dependency 上**。

⟹ **`Memory Dependency 11.3%` 严重低估了真实的访存等待:**
```
Memory Dependency   11.3%
Stall AMC            9.1%   ← cp.async 的 wait_group
Stall Sync 的一部分  ≤23.6% ← 等最慢 warp 的 copy
                    ──────
真实访存侧          20.4% ~ 44%
```

这也解释了 %HBM 只有 18.5% —— **它在等内存,只是等在了 barrier 上,读 stall 表时看不出来。**

## 一个我该收回的数

我两次引用了 codex 的「128 peers」。**按这个 shape 算不出 128:**
```
32 n-tile × 32 k-tile = 1024 个 k-tile-step
bpc1 72 CTA  →  每 CTA 14.2 个  →  一个输出 tile(32 k-tile)需要 32/14.2 = 2.25 个 peer
```
**C-chain 只有 2-3 深,不是 128。** codex 那个数(`128 × 128 × 4 = 65,536 B`)算术自洽,但我对不上它的 shape 假设 —— **单独列着,不调和**。这需要问它 S=4 和 128 各指什么。

## 对杠杆的影响

**主循环的 barrier 次数是不变量:**
```
wait_stage 总次数 = 每 CTA 处理的 k-tile 数
                  与 Stages 无关(Stages 小 → 每 while 少,但 while 多)
                  与展开无关(173 那个 pragma 一次都不减)
```

⟹ **要减主循环 barrier,只有两条:**
```
每 CTA 少拿 k-tile   →  更深的 split-K  →  peer 链更长(②ↃStall Sync)  —— 拆东墙补西墙
去掉 barrier 本身    →  per-warp 的 cp.async 等待,不做 CTA 级 rendezvous
                        —— 但那要求 warp 之间不共享 shared stage,即 warp 独立流水
```

第二条正是 **D9 那条路的形状**(1 warp/CTA ⟹ `__syncthreads()` 退化成空操作)。**这可能是 46.0% vs 18.5% 里被低估的一环** —— 我一直把它当「occupancy 轴」,但它同时是「barrier 轴」。

⟹ 上一轮那个梯度里,**「warps/CTA」这一列要拆成两个后果记录:寄存器量化 和 barrier 耦合。** 步骤 ②(WK=2,走 K 方向长出第二个 warp)第一次让 `__syncthreads()` 变成真的 —— **那一步的 Stall Sync 变化是整个梯度里信息量最大的一个读数。**
